Questions and answers

Q: What is What's?

A: What's = What is. I'm = I am.

Q: How do I say my name?

A: My name is Ana. or I'm Ana. Both are good.

Q: First name or last name?

A: Ana = first name. Ruiz = last name (family name). In English, the first name comes first: Ana Ruiz.

Q: How do I spell my name?

A: Say each letter in English, with a short stop: R… U… I… Z.

Q: I don't understand. What do I say?

A: Can you repeat, please? or I don't understand.

Practice: Write the missing word.

Español: Escribe la palabra que falta.

  4. Can you ____________, please? Yes. V-E-G-A.
  5. Are you a student? Yes, I ____________.

✗ Don't say✓ Say

What's = What is (¿Cuál es…?). Di My name is Ana o I'm Ana (no «I call me Ana»). Siempre usa is o 'm: no «My name Ana».

Tip for speakers of other languages: In English, the first name comes first and the family name comes last: Ana Ruiz. Always use is or 'm in these answers: My name is Ana. I'm Ana.

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. The student pages have a Spanish line and a "My language" line for every task. Learners read those on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Listen or write?"), then go. Say less, show more. Use the same short words every time: Listen. Repeat. Point. Circle. Write. Partner. Group.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the instruction and the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 1 (Week 1): Hello! What's Your Name?

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • say hello and goodbye (Hello. Hi. Goodbye. See you next week.)
  • say their first and last name (My name is Ana. I'm Ana. My last name is Ruiz.)
  • ask and answer What's your name? How do you spell it? and spell their name aloud
  • ask for help: Can you repeat, please?
  • say and write the letters of the alphabet (Letters & Numbers block)

Materials

  • name tags and markers
  • Student Pages for Lesson 1 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • a big alphabet strip (or write A–Z on the board before class)
  • a sign-in sheet page for each learner (Talk Time page)
  • mini whiteboards or scrap paper for Letters & Numbers
  • baseline snapshot checklist (in the answer key)
  • phone + small speaker, L1_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 30 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ hello • ★ goodbye • ★ name • ★ first name • ★ last name • ★ spell • letter • ★ teacher • ★ student • classmate • book • pen

Classroom phrases (poster page, no pictures needed)

Listen. • Repeat. • Write. • Can you repeat, please? • I don't understand. • How do you say ___ in English?

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take the time from Grammar or Talk Time. The last 15 minutes are the Letters & Numbers block.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. Print for the number you expect, plus 3 spares. Late arrivals join any pair or circle right away.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Welcome + Hello Circle · 10 min

  • Grouping: two circles (15 learners) / one circle (7–8 learners). Stand.
  • Before class: write on the board: Hello! My name is ___ . Each learner writes a first name on a name tag.
  • Model: wave and say, "Hello! My name is (your name)." Point to yourself. Then point to a learner and wait. Help with "My name is…".
  • Do: around the circle, each person says "Hello! My name is ___." The group answers "Hello, ___!"
  • Round 2: the same with "I'm ___." Point to the board: My name is = I'm.
  • Late arrivals: join a circle. Give them a name tag.
  • If behind: go around once only.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:15 · Orientation: How Our Class Works · 5 min

  • Grouping: whole class. Open the Student Pages to How Our Class Works.
  • Show the times: point to the clock and the page: class 6:00, break 6:45, back 7:00, end 7:30.
  • Show the instruction words: say each word and do the action: (hand to ear) "Listen." "Say." (mime writing) "Write." (point to two people) "Partner." Learners copy your gesture.
  • Say: "Write your language here," and point to a "My language" line. Learners can fill it in now or at home. No one has to.
  • The 3 rules (say and show): (1) "English in class. A classmate can help you for a few seconds. Then back to English." (2) "Homework every week. It's short." (3) "Phones are OK for the audio and a dictionary."
  • Also say: "You can use a real name or a practice name." (See Teacher notes.)
  • If behind: say the 3 rules only.

Step 3 · 6:15–6:25 · New Words · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: the New Words page. Hold up a real book and a real pen first.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat twice. Say each word slowly and clearly. Act out hello (wave), goodbye (wave and walk to the door), spell (write A-N-A in the air).
  • first name / last name: write your own name on the board. Point to the first part: "First name." Point to the second part: "Last name." Do the same with 2 learners' names.
  • Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then switch. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
  • Classroom phrases (2 min): turn to the Classroom Phrases page. Say each phrase with its gesture; learners repeat. Practice "Can you repeat, please?" right away: say a word too fast, and wait for someone to ask.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only. The other words stay on the page for home study.

Step 4 · 6:25–6:35 · Listening + "Say it" · 10 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): point to the pictures of Ana and Carlos. Say: "This is Ana. This is Carlos. First night. They say their names. They spell their names."
  • Listen 1 → Task A (check Ana or Carlos). Pause after Ana spells her name, and ask the class to point: "Ana or Carlos?"
  • Listen 2 → Task B (circle the letters). Listen 3 → Task C (write the two last names).
  • Pairs compare after each task: "Show your partner." Then show the answers on the board.
  • "Say it" (2 min): play or read 2 lines: "How do you spell it?" and "Can you repeat, please?" The class repeats each line twice. Use a flat, clear voice; then make it friendly.
  • The audio plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen.
  • If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together on the board.

Step 5 · 6:35–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer. Point left, then right.
  • Q&A: you read a question from the left side. The class reads an answer from the right side. Do Box 1 and Box 2 like this, then Box 3.
  • Say and write on the board: "What's = What is. I'm = I am."
  • Box 4 (2 min, a first look): "Are you a student?" Class: "Yes, I am." Point to yourself: "Am I a student?" Class: "No, you're not. You're a teacher!" Don't teach more; Lesson 2 does.
  • Check questions: "My name ___ Ana." (is) • "How do you ___ it?" (spell) • "Are you a teacher?" (No, I'm not.)
  • Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks from the left side; B answers from the right side with real information (or a practice name). Then switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices the same questions.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Put the sign-in sheets on the tables. Write on the board: What's your name? How do you spell it? Can you repeat, please?

Step 6 · 7:00–7:10 · Talk Time: Name Mingle with the Sign-In Sheet · 10 min

  • Grouping: mingle. 15 learners: talk to 5–6 people. 7–8 learners: talk to everyone.
  • Model with one learner: "Hello! What's your name?" → "Rosa." "How do you spell it?" → "R-O-S-A." Write R-O-S-A on the board as you hear it. Then show your paper to the learner: "Is this right?" → "Yes!"
  • Do: learners stand, greet, ask, and write the first and last name on the sign-in sheet as the partner spells it. The partner looks and checks ✓ the spelling. Then they say "Goodbye!" and find a new person.
  • Help phrases: point to the board when someone is stuck: "Can you repeat, please?"
  • Baseline snapshot: while learners mingle, the teacher (or a second volunteer) calls about 5 learners, one at a time, for 2 minutes and uses the checklist in the answer key. Do the rest in Weeks 2 and 3.
  • With 5 or fewer learners: sit at one table and go around; everyone writes everyone's name.
  • If behind: learners talk to 3 people.

Step 7 · 7:10–7:15 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner says one sentence to you at the door ("My name is ___. ___-___-___.") or writes one sentence on a slip (My name is ___.). Copying from the grammar box is fine.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together. Point to each instruction so learners know what to do at home.

Letters & Numbers · 7:15–7:25 · The Alphabet · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page and the alphabet on the board.
  • See it (2 min): point to each letter on the board, A to Z. Say each letter once. Point to a capital and its small letter: "Big A, small a."
  • Say it (4 min): learners repeat A to Z after you, in groups of 4–5 letters (A B C D, E F G, H I J K…). Then go to the tricky letters box. Say each letter 3 times, slowly, with its English example word. Spend the most time on A / E / I and G / J.
  • Quick check (1 min): say a tricky letter; learners point to it on their page. Say: "E." (They point to E, not I.) "G." (G, not J.)
  • Write it (3 min): Task B: say the 5 practice letters (the list is in the answer key). Learners circle them. Then Task C: learners write their name in capital letters and small letters.
  • Partners: Task D: A spells their name; B writes it on a whiteboard or paper. A checks. Switch.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they say the letters with everyone, point instead of circle, and copy their name from their name tag. A helper, if you have one, sits with them.
  • If behind: do the tricky letters and Task D only.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · First can-do self-check · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 5 letters (answer key), slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle.
  • Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 2). It shows who needs more help with letters.
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 2 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L1_listening.mp3 (about 1:16; the conversation plays once, so play the audio again if needed)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Read slowly and spell each letter clearly, with a short pause between letters.

Narrator: Lesson one. Listening. It's the first night of English class. Ana and Carlos sign in. Listen.

Receptionist: Hello! Welcome to English class.

Ana: Hello. Thank you.

Receptionist: What's your name?

Ana: My name is Ana.

Receptionist: Hi, Ana. What's your last name?

Ana: It's Ruiz.

Receptionist: How do you spell it?

Ana: R, U, I, Z.

Receptionist: Thank you, Ana. Next, please! Hello! What's your name?

Carlos: Hi. I'm Carlos. My last name is Vega.

Receptionist: How do you spell it?

Carlos: V, E, G, A.

Receptionist: Sorry. Can you repeat, please?

Carlos: Yes, of course. V, E, G, A.

Receptionist: Thank you, Carlos. How are you?

Carlos: I'm fine, thanks. And you?

Receptionist: I'm fine, thank you. Here's your book and a pen.

Carlos: Thank you. Goodbye!

Receptionist: Goodbye!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: 1 Ana, 2 Carlos, 3 Carlos, 4 Carlos.
  • Listening Task B: Ana: R U I Z • Carlos: V E G A.
  • Listening Task C: RUIZ (Ana) • VEGA (Carlos).
  • Grammar practice (Write the missing word): 1 name, 2 What's, 3 spell, 4 repeat, 5 am.
  • Homework 3 (write the word): 1 book, 2 pen, 3 teacher, 4 student.
  • Letters & Numbers Task B (the teacher says): 1 E, 2 G, 3 I, 4 J, 5 A. Say each letter 2 times.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says): 1 I, 2 J, 3 E, 4 H, 5 G. Say each letter 2 times.
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 c, 2 d, 3 a, 4 b.
  • Progress Check scoring: Part A /5 + Part B /4 + Part C /2 = /11. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs help with letters (Part A) and with reading the questions (Part B).

Baseline snapshot checklist (Weeks 1–3)

Ask the 6 prompts, in this order. Check ✓ if the learner answers without help. Write ~ if they answer with help. Leave it empty if not yet. The final exam uses the same prompts.

LearnerWhat's your name?How do you spell it?Where are you from?What's your phone number?Do you have kids?What do you do?





Learners can give a practice phone number (555-0100 to 555-0199) instead of a real one. Never write down real phone numbers.

Teacher notes

  • Names and privacy: every learner may use a practice name in class (for example, a name from the listening). Never ask for immigration status, money, or a real address. Practice phone numbers start with 555-01 (for example, 555-0142).
  • Spelling names: write each name on the board exactly as you hear it. If you write the wrong letter, that is useful: the class sees which letter names are not clear yet. Smile, ask "Can you repeat, please?", and fix it together.
  • The letters learners mix up most: A / E / I (in English, E sounds like "ee" and I sounds like "eye"), G / J, H ("aych"), Y ("why"), W ("double-u"), and V / B. When you say these, say them slowly, and point to the letter.
  • First name and last name: in some cultures the family name comes first, and some learners have two last names. Say: "In the U.S., forms want the first name first." Two last names are fine. Learners write both, or the one they use on forms.
  • Mixed levels: learners who already know the alphabet spell longer names (a city, a street) in Talk Time and help a partner. New learners use the grammar box as a script.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they take part fully in all the speaking. In reading and writing tasks, they point instead of circle, and copy from the board or their name tag. Don't make them read aloud.
  • Typical mistakes this week: My name Ana (no is), I Ana (no 'm), and saying the Spanish names of the letters (E said as "eh," I said as "ee"). Correct by saying the right form clearly; the learner repeats. Learners can read the note on their Grammar page themselves; you don't need to explain it.

Q: am, is, or are?

A: I → am. he, she, it → is. you, we, they → are.

Q: Can I say Is from Mexico?

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. The student pages have a Spanish line and a "My language" line for every task. Learners read those on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Listen or write?"), then go. Say less, show more. Use the same short words every time: Listen. Repeat. Point. Circle. Write. Partner. Group.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the instruction and the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Lesson 2 (Week 2): Where Are You From?

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • say where they are from (I'm from Mexico. I'm from Guadalajara.)
  • ask where someone is from (Where are you from? Where is she from? What city?)
  • answer yes/no questions with be (Is he from Honduras? Yes, he is. / No, he isn't.)
  • say an age with be (I'm 35. He's 12.), not with have
  • say, understand, and write the numbers 0–20 (Letters & Numbers block)

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 2 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • a world map (paper, or on a screen) and small sticky notes or stickers
  • name tags from Week 1 (and markers for new learners)
  • mini whiteboards or scrap paper for Letters & Numbers
  • number cards 0–20 (or write 0–20 on the board before class)
  • baseline snapshot checklist (in the answer key; continue from Week 1)
  • phone + small speaker, L1_L2_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 30 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ country • ★ city • ★ Mexico • ★ Guatemala • ★ Honduras • ★ El Salvador • Colombia • ★ the United States • ★ he • ★ she • ★ they • ★ How old?

Review from Lesson 1

What's your name? How do you spell it? How are you? Can you repeat, please? • Are you a student? Yes, I am.

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take the time from Grammar or Talk Time. The last 15 minutes are the Letters & Numbers block.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
6:00–6:10Hello + Review (Lesson 1 questions) + homework check10Pairs, then new pairsOne partner only
6:10–6:20New Words (picture page) + pair picture game10Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:20–6:32Listening (audio) + "Say it"12Individuals, then pairs checkPlay the audio 2 times, not 3
6:32–6:45Grammar Q&A: Where are you from? Is she from…? How old…? + pair drill13Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; it becomes homework
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:10Talk Time: Class Map (interview, introduce a partner, map) + baseline snapshot10Pairs, then groups of 3–4 / pairs, then one groupSkip the map stickers
7:10–7:15Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:15–7:25Letters & Numbers: numbers 0–20 (See it → Say it → Write it)10Whole class, then pairsDo Tasks A and B only
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it in Week 3 at 6:00, while people arrive

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the third play of the audio; (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time. Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. Print for the number you expect, plus 3 spares. Late arrivals join any pair right away. New learners this week: give them a name tag and pair them with a strong partner.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Hello + Review · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
  • Before class: write on the board: What's your name? How do you spell it? How are you? Are you a student?
  • Model with one learner: "Hello! What's your name?" → "Rosa." "How do you spell it?" → "R-O-S-A." "How are you?" → "I'm fine, thanks. And you?"
  • Do: pairs use the Hello + Review page. A asks the 4 questions; B answers. Then switch. Then find a new partner and do it again.
  • Homework check (last 3 min): partners show each other their Lesson 1 homework (the name, the friend's name, the 4 words). Walk around and look. Collect any Lesson 1 Progress Checks that were not done.
  • New learners: pair them with a strong partner. They can do the Lesson 1 Progress Check at home.
  • If behind: one partner only.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:20 · New Words · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: the New Words page (or the world map). Point to a country on the map, then to the flag on the page: "Mexico. This is a country."
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat twice. Stress the strong part of each word: MEX-i-co, gua-te-MA-la, hon-DU-ras, el SAL-va-dor, co-LOM-bi-a, the u-NI-ted STATES.
  • country / city: "Mexico is a country. Guadalajara is a city." Say two more: "Honduras: country. Tegucigalpa: city."
  • he / she / they: point to a man in the room: "he." A woman: "she." A group: "they." Learners point as you say the word (fast, like a game).
  • How old?: point to the cake. "How old? … 12. 20. 35." Hold up fingers.
  • Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then switch. Then: A points to a classmate, B says he or she.
  • Learners from other countries: write their country on the board and say it together. Every country is welcome; the page has the 6 most common in this program.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:20–6:32 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "This is Rosa. This is Marco. They are new students. It's the break." Point to the flags in Task A: "Where are they from? Listen."
  • Listen 1 → Task A (match the person and the flag; write the letter).
  • Listen 2 → Task B (Yes or No, 4 pictures). Listen 3 → Task C (write the age).
  • Pairs compare after each task: "Show your partner." Then show the answers on the board.
  • "Say it" (2 min): read 2 lines: "Where are you from?" and "How old is he?" The class repeats each line twice. Then pairs ask and answer each other.
  • The audio plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen.
  • If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together on the board.

Step 4 · 6:32–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 13 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer. Point left, then right.
  • Box 1: you read a question; the class reads an answer. Point to a learner: "Where is he from?" → "He's from…".
  • Box 2: ask about learners in the room: "Is Rosa from Mexico?" → "No, she isn't. She's from Guatemala." Stress the short answers: Yes, she is. No, she isn't.
  • Box 3 (2 min): read the long form; the class reads the short form. Write on the board: I → am. he, she, it → is. you, we, they → are.
  • Box 4: "How old are you?" Answer for yourself (a real or a practice age). Write: I'm 35. Then write I have 35 years and draw a big ✗ on it.
  • Check questions: "She ___ from Colombia." (is) • "Where ___ they from?" (are) • "Is he from Mexico? No, he ___." (isn't)
  • Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks from the left side about B or about a classmate; B answers from the right side. Then switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. It becomes homework, and Talk Time practices the same questions.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Put up the world map. Write on the board: Where are you from? What city? This is ___. He's / She's from ___.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:10 · Talk Time: Class Map · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs, then groups of 3–4. 7–8 learners: pairs, then one group (the whole class).
  • Model with one learner: "Where are you from?" → "Honduras." "What city?" → "San Pedro Sula." Write it in the table on the board. Then turn to the class: "This is Marco. He's from Honduras. He's from San Pedro Sula."
  • Part 1 (3 min): pairs interview each other and write the partner's name, country, and city on the Talk Time page.
  • Part 2 (4 min): each pair joins another pair. Each learner introduces the partner: "This is ___. He's / She's from ___." The group asks one question: "What city?" or "Is she from ___?"
  • Part 3 (2 min): each learner puts a sticky note with their name on the map (or the teacher writes the names on the board under each country).
  • Any country is OK. Learners can choose a city or country they like. Never ask how or why someone came here.
  • Baseline snapshot: while groups talk, call about 5 learners you didn't check in Week 1, one at a time, for 2 minutes. Use the checklist in the answer key.
  • If behind: skip Part 3.

Step 6 · 7:10–7:15 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner says one sentence to you at the door ("I'm from ___." or "This is ___. She's from ___.") or writes one sentence on a slip. Copying from the grammar box is fine.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together. Point to each instruction so learners know what to do at home.

Letters & Numbers · 7:15–7:25 · Numbers 0–20 · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page and the numbers on the board.
  • See it (2 min): point to each number, 0 to 20, and say it once. Hold up fingers for 0–10.
  • Say it (3 min): learners repeat 0–10, then 11–20. Then go to the tricky numbers box. Say each one 3 times. Spend the most time on 3 (th: tongue between the teeth), 13 / 14…19 (stress the end: thir-TEEN), 12 / 20 (twelve, twenty), and 7 (v, not b).
  • Quick check (1 min): say a number; learners hold up fingers or point on the page.
  • Write it (3 min): Task B: say the 5 numbers in the answer key, 2 times each. Learners circle. Task C: read the 3 ages (answer key). Learners write numbers, not words. Task D: learners write the sentence again with capital letters (Maria, Colombia).
  • Partners: Task E: A says a number from 0 to 20; B writes it. A checks. Switch.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they say the numbers with everyone, hold up fingers, and point instead of circle. A helper, if you have one, sits with them.
  • If behind: do Tasks A and B only.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 5 numbers (answer key), slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle.
  • Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 3). Part A shows who needs more help with numbers.
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 3 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L1_L2_listening.mp3 (about 1:17; the conversation plays once, so play the audio again if needed)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Read slowly, with a short stop between speakers.

Narrator: Lesson two. Listening. It's the break at English class. Rosa and Marco are new students. Listen.

Rosa: Hi! I'm Rosa. What's your name?

Marco: Hi, Rosa. I'm Marco. Nice to meet you.

Rosa: Nice to meet you, too. Where are you from, Marco?

Marco: I'm from Mexico.

Rosa: Oh, nice! What city?

Marco: Guadalajara. And you? Are you from Mexico, too?

Rosa: No, I'm not. I'm from El Salvador.

Marco: Oh, OK. What city?

Rosa: San Salvador. My son is here, too. He's in the kids' class.

Marco: Oh, how old is he?

Rosa: He's twelve years old.

Marco: Twelve? That's great. My friends are here, too. They're from Honduras.

Rosa: Is the teacher from Mexico?

Marco: No, she isn't. She's from the United States.

Rosa: OK. Time for class! See you later, Marco.

Marco: See you later!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: 1 Rosa b (El Salvador), 2 Marco a (Mexico), 3 the friends d (Honduras), 4 the teacher c (the United States).
  • Listening Task B: 1 Yes, 2 No (Rosa is from El Salvador), 3 Yes, 4 No (the teacher is from the United States).
  • Listening Task C: 12 (twelve).
  • Grammar practice (Write am, is, or are): 1 am, 2 is, 3 are, 4 Is / is, 5 are, 6 are.
  • Homework 2 (am, is, are): 1 am, 2 is, 3 are, 4 is, 5 are.
  • Homework 3 (the country): 1 Mexico, 2 Colombia, 3 Honduras, 4 the United States.
  • Letters & Numbers Task B (the teacher says): 1 12, 2 3, 3 15, 4 7, 5 20. Say each number 2 times.
  • Letters & Numbers Task C (the teacher says): 1 "He's 9." 2 "She's 14." 3 "They're 18 and 20." Say each one 2 times.
  • Letters & Numbers Task D: Maria is from Colombia.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says): 1 13, 2 6, 3 20, 4 11, 5 17. Say each number 2 times.
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 c, 2 d, 3 a, 4 b.
  • Progress Check Part C: 1 am, 2 is, 3 are.
  • Progress Check scoring: Part A /5 + Part B /4 + Part C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs help with numbers (Part A) and with am / is / are (Parts B and C).

Baseline snapshot checklist (Weeks 1–3, continued)

Use the same sheet as Week 1, or this copy. Ask the 6 prompts, in this order. Check ✓ if the learner answers without help. Write ~ if they answer with help. Leave it empty if not yet. The final exam uses the same prompts.

LearnerWhat's your name?How do you spell it?Where are you from?What's your phone number?Do you have kids?What do you do?





Learners can give a practice phone number (555-0100 to 555-0199) instead of a real one. Never write down real phone numbers.

Teacher notes

  • Countries and privacy: learners can talk about any country or city: where they were born, where they lived, or a place they like. Never ask about immigration, papers, or how or why someone came to the U.S. If a learner doesn't want to answer, "I'm from (this city)" is a fine answer.
  • Age is optional: some adults don't like to say their age. In Box 4 and in the listening, practice with children's ages and invented ages. Say: "You can say a practice age."
  • The big mistake this week: Spanish can leave out the person (Es de México). English can't. Listen for Is from Mexico and give back She's from Mexico. The second big mistake is I have 35 years → I'm 35. Learners can read the Spanish note on their Grammar page; you don't need to explain it.
  • the United States: say the United States (or the U.S.). Other countries on the page have no the: Mexico, Honduras.
  • Short answers: Yes, she is. (never Yes, she's.) • No, she isn't. or No, she's not. Both are correct; the page teaches isn't.
  • Mixed levels: strong learners add the city (I'm from Mexico. I'm from Puebla.) and ask a second question in Talk Time. New learners use the grammar box as a script.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they take part fully in the speaking. In writing tasks, they point and circle, and copy the country from the New Words page. Don't make them read aloud.
  • Looking ahead: Lesson 3 adds his / her (Her name is Rosa. His phone number is…) and numbers to 100. Lesson 4 adds Do you have kids?

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. The student pages have a Spanish line and a "My language" line for every task. Learners read those on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Listen or write?"), then go. Say less, show more. Use the same short words every time: Listen. Repeat. Point. Circle. Write. Partner. Group.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the instruction and the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Privacy this week: learners never need to give a real phone number or address. Every activity works with the practice ID cards and practice numbers (555-0100 to 555-0199). Say this at the start of class.

Lesson 3 (Week 3): My Phone Number and Address

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • say and understand a phone number (It's 555-0142. Five-five-five, oh-one-four-two.)
  • say an address (It's 210 Pine Street, Apartment 3.)
  • ask What's your phone number? What's your address? and Can you repeat, please?
  • use my / your / his / her / our / their (Her phone number is… His address is…)
  • fill out a simple form in capital letters and sign it
  • say and write numbers to 100, and hear 13 vs. 30 (Letters & Numbers block)

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 3 (print for the number expected + 3 spares). Talk Time: print the Student A page for half the class and the Student B page for the other half.
  • one real paper form to show (a library card or clinic sign-in form, with no one's information on it)
  • mini whiteboards or scrap paper for Letters & Numbers
  • number cards 13–19 and 30–90 (or write them on the board)
  • baseline snapshot checklist (in the answer key; finish it this week)
  • phone + small speaker, L1_L3_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 30 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ phone number • ★ address • ★ street • apartment (Apt.) • ★ city • ★ ZIP code • ★ email • ★ form • ★ signature • ID card • ★ zero ("oh") • numbers 21–100

Review from Lessons 1–2

How do you spell it? Can you repeat, please? • Where are you from? Is she from Mexico? Yes, she is. • How old is he? • numbers 0–20

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take the time from Grammar or Talk Time. The last 15 minutes are the Letters & Numbers block.

6:10–6:20New Words (picture page) + pair picture game10Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the third play of the audio; (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time. Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. Print for the number you expect, plus 3 spares. Late arrivals join any pair right away. In Talk Time, an A always works with a B; with an odd number, two Bs share one A.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Hello + Review · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
  • Before class: write on the board: Where are you from? What city? Where is he / she from? Is he / she from ___?
  • Model with one learner: "Where are you from?" → "Guatemala." "What city?" → "Antigua." Then point to another learner: "Where is she from?" → "She's from Mexico."
  • Do: pairs use the Hello + Review page. A asks; B answers. Then they ask about a classmate (Where is he from? Is she from Honduras?). Switch. Then find a new partner.
  • Homework check (last 3 min): partners show each other their Lesson 2 homework. Walk around and look at item 2 (am / is / are).
  • New learners: pair them with a strong partner. They can do the Lesson 1–2 Progress Checks at home.
  • If behind: one partner only.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:20 · New Words · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Say first: "This is practice. You don't need your real phone number or your real address."
  • Show: a real paper form (no one's information on it). Point to the lines: "This is a form. First name. Last name. Phone number. Address."
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat twice. Act out signature (sign your name in the air) and email (type on a phone).
  • zero = "oh": write 555-0142 on the board. Say it slowly in groups: "five-five-five… oh-one-four-two." Point to the 0: "Oh. In phone numbers, 0 is often oh."
  • numbers 21–100: point to the tiles and say them. Learners repeat. (Letters & Numbers practices them more.)
  • Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then switch. Then: A points to a line on the form picture, B says the word (city, ZIP code…).
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:20–6:32 · Listening + "Say it" · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "This is Ana. She's at a clinic. She's a new patient. The receptionist asks: What's your phone number? What's your address?" Point to the form in Task B.
  • Listen 1 → Task A (circle the right number: phone, street, apartment, ZIP code).
  • Listen 2 → Task B (fill out Ana's form). Listen 3 → Task C (check what Ana writes) and finish Task B.
  • Pairs compare after each task: "Show your partner." Then write the answers on the board.
  • "Say it" (2 min): no student page needed. Write 2 lines on the board (they are also in Grammar Box 3): "What's your phone number?" and "Can you repeat, please?" The class repeats each line twice. Then pairs ask and answer with a practice number.
  • The audio plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen.
  • If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.

Step 4 · 6:32–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 13 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer. Point left, then right.
  • Box 1: you read a question; the class reads an answer.
  • Box 2 (the key point): point to a man: "his phone number." Point to a woman: "her phone number." Point to yourself: "my." To a learner: "your." To the class and you: "our class." To two learners: "their city." Write on the board: he → his. she → her.
  • Box 3: read a wrong number on purpose: "Is your phone number 555-0124?" → "No, it isn't. It's 555-0142."
  • Box 4: read the left side; the class reads the right side. Say the groups with a small stop: 555 … 0142.
  • Check questions: point to a man: "What's ___ name?" (his) • to a woman: (her) • "I'm Ana. ___ last name is Ruiz." (My)
  • Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks from the left side about a person in the pictures (Ana, Carlos); B answers from the right side. Then switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. It becomes homework, and Talk Time practices the same questions.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Put the Student A and Student B pages in two piles. Write on the board: What's your phone number? What's your address? Can you repeat, please? How do you spell it?

Step 5 · 7:00–7:10 · Talk Time: Information Gap with Practice ID Cards · 10 min

  • Grouping: A–B pairs. Give half the class the Student A page and half the Student B page. With an odd number, two Bs share one A. Partners don't show their pages.
  • Model with one learner (you are A): "What's your first name?" → "Marco." "How do you spell your last name?" → "S-I-L-V-A." Write it on the board as you hear it. "What's your phone number?" → "555-0163." "Can you repeat, please?"
  • Part 1 (5 min): A asks and writes B's information on the form. Then B asks and writes A's information.
  • Part 2 (2 min): partners show their pages and check: is the form the same as the ID card? Fix any mistakes together.
  • Part 3 (2 min): pairs join another pair. Each learner says 2 sentences about the partner's card: "Her name is Rosa Diaz. Her phone number is 555-0187." / "His address is 1850 Lake Avenue."
  • Fast pairs: do it again with their own information only if they want to, or with an invented card.
  • Baseline snapshot: while pairs work, call the last learners you haven't checked, one at a time, for 2 minutes. Use the checklist in the answer key. This is the last week of the baseline.
  • If behind: skip Part 3.

Step 6 · 7:10–7:15 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner says a phone number (a practice number is fine: "My phone number is 555-01__.") or writes one sentence with his or her (Her phone number is 555-0187.). Copying is fine.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (the first two lines of the form). Point to each instruction so learners know what to do at home.

Letters & Numbers · 7:15–7:25 · Numbers to 100, -teen / -ty, Forms · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page.
  • See it (1 min): point to 20, 30, 40… 100 on the page and say each one.
  • Say it (3 min): go to the -teen / -ty box. Say each pair 3 times: "thir-TEEN… THIR-ty." Clap on the strong part. -teen is long and strong at the end; -ty is short and strong at the start. Learners show 1 finger + 3 for 13 and 3 fingers + a circle (0) for 30.
  • Quick check (1 min): say 14 or 40, 15 or 50… Learners point on the page.
  • Write it (4 min): Task B: say the 5 numbers in the answer key, 2 times each. Learners circle. Task C: read the 2 practice phone numbers in groups (five-five-five… oh-one-six-three). Learners write them. Task D: learners copy the card into the form in CAPITAL letters.
  • Partners: A says a practice phone number (555-01__), B writes it. A checks. Switch.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they say the numbers with everyone and point. In Task D they copy only the first name and last name. A helper, if you have one, sits with them.
  • If behind: do Tasks A and B only.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 5 numbers (answer key), slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle.
  • Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 4). Part A shows who still mixes up -teen and -ty.
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 4 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L1_L3_listening.mp3 (about 1:05; the conversation plays once, so play the audio again if needed)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Read the numbers slowly, in groups, with a short stop: five-five-five… oh-one-four-two.

Narrator: Lesson three. Listening. Ana is at a clinic. She is a new patient. Listen.

Receptionist: Good morning. Can I help you?

Ana: Hi. I'm a new patient. My name is Ana Ruiz.

Receptionist: OK, Ana. What's your phone number?

Ana: It's 555-0142. (five-five-five, oh-one-four-two)

Receptionist: Sorry. Can you repeat, please?

Ana: Sure. 555-0142.

Receptionist: Thank you. And what's your address?

Ana: It's 210 Pine Street, Apartment 3. (two-ten Pine Street)

Receptionist: 210 Pine Street, Apartment 3. What's the city?

Ana: Riverside. The ZIP code is 54107. (five-four-one-oh-seven)

Receptionist: Thank you. Please write your email here. And sign here, please.

Ana: OK. Here you go.

Receptionist: Thank you, Ana. Please sit down.

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: 1 555-0142, 2 210, 3 3, 4 54107.
  • Listening Task B (Ana's form): Last name: RUIZ • Phone number: 555-0142 • Address: 210 Pine Street, Apt. 3 • City: RIVERSIDE • ZIP code: 54107.
  • Listening Task C: ✓ email, ✓ signature (not an ID card).
  • Grammar practice (Write my, your, his, or her): 1 my, 2 His, 3 Her, 4 your, 5 her.
  • Homework 2 (my, your, his, her, our, their): 1 My, 2 His, 3 Her, 4 Our, 5 Their.
  • Homework 3 (write the number): 1 30, 2 14, 3 50, 4 99, 5 100.
  • Letters & Numbers Task B (the teacher says): 1 30, 2 14, 3 50, 4 16, 5 90. Say each number 2 times.
  • Letters & Numbers Task C (the teacher says): 1 555-0163 ("five-five-five, oh-one-six-three"), 2 555-0118 ("five-five-five, oh-one-one-eight"). Say each one 2 times, in groups.
  • Letters & Numbers Task D: FIRST NAME: ROSA • LAST NAME: DIAZ • STREET: 46 OAK STREET • CITY: RIVERSIDE.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says): 1 13, 2 40, 3 15, 4 70, 5 80. Say each number 2 times.
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 b, 2 d, 3 a, 4 c.
  • Progress Check Part C: 1 His, 2 Her, 3 My.
  • Progress Check scoring: Part A /5 + Part B /4 + Part C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. Part A shows who needs more help with -teen / -ty; Part C shows his / her.

Baseline snapshot checklist (Weeks 1–3, last week)

Use the same sheet as Weeks 1–2, or this copy. Ask the 6 prompts, in this order. Check ✓ if the learner answers without help. Write ~ if they answer with help. Leave it empty if not yet. The final exam uses the same prompts.

LearnerWhat's your name?How do you spell it?Where are you from?What's your phone number?Do you have kids?What do you do?





Learners can give a practice phone number (555-0100 to 555-0199) instead of a real one. Never write down real phone numbers.

Teacher notes

  • Privacy: never ask for or write down a real phone number, address, or email. The practice ID cards and the 555-01__ numbers are for class. If a learner wants to use real information, that's their choice, but don't collect it.
  • The big mistake this week: his and her. Spanish uses su for both. In English, his is for a man and her is for a woman; the word depends on the person, not the thing. Correct by pointing to the person: "Carlos… his." Learners can read the Spanish note on their Grammar page; you don't need to explain it.
  • Phone numbers: say one digit at a time, in groups (3 + 4), with a short stop between the groups. 0 is usually "oh." 555-0100 = "five-five-five, oh-one-hundred" is also common, but teach digit by digit for now.
  • Street numbers: usually in pairs: 210 = "two-ten," 1850 = "eighteen-fifty," 46 = "forty-six." The number comes before the street name: 210 Pine Street (not Pine Street 210).
  • -teen or -ty? This is the hardest number pair for everyone. When a learner says 13 and you hear 30 (or the opposite), ask: "One-three or three-zero?" and write both on the board.
  • Spelling review: in Talk Time, learners spell names and streets. Point to the Lesson 1 tricky letters (A / E / I, G / J) when you hear a mistake.
  • Mixed levels: strong learners add the email and spell it (a-n-a at mail dot com). New learners use the box What's your ___? It's ___. for every line of the form.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they take part fully in the speaking. On forms, they copy their first and last name and a practice number from the card. Don't make them read aloud.
  • Looking ahead: Lesson 4 uses his / her with family (This is my sister. Her name is Ana.) and the first do question: Do you have kids?

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. The student pages have a Spanish line and a "My language" line for every task. Learners read those on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Listen or write?"), then go. Say less, show more. Use the same short words every time: Listen. Repeat. Point. Circle. Write. Partner. Group.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the instruction and the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Family can be a sensitive topic. Some learners have family far away, have lost family members, or don't want to talk about their family. Every activity works with the picture-card family (Ana's family), and you say this at the start: "You can talk about your family or Ana's family." Married / single is optional: never ask a learner directly if they are married.

Lesson 4 (Week 4): This Is My Family

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • name family members (mother, father, son, daughter, brother, sister…)
  • say This is my brother. His name is Luis. He's 25.
  • ask and answer Who's this? and How old is he / she?
  • ask and answer Do you have kids? Yes, I do. I have two. / No, I don't.
  • use 's (Ana's husband, Carlos's son)
  • hear and say short vowels (dad, mom, son, kids) and write plural -s (Letters & Numbers block)

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 4 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • optional: one photo of your own family (or of a family from a magazine). Learners may show a photo on their phone, but never ask them to.
  • a big family tree drawn on the board (copy the blank tree on the Talk Time page)
  • mini whiteboards or scrap paper for Letters & Numbers
  • phone + small speaker, L1_L4_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 30 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ mother • ★ father • ★ parents • ★ husband • ★ wife • ★ son • ★ daughter • ★ children (kids) • baby • grandmother • grandfather • family • brother • sister

Review from Lessons 1–3

What's your / his / her phone number? It's… • How old is he? He's 12. • Is she from Mexico? Yes, she is. • numbers 0–100

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take the time from Grammar or Talk Time. The last 15 minutes are the Letters & Numbers block.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind

6:10–6:20New Words (picture page) + pair picture game10Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:20–6:32Listening (audio): Carlos shows Kim his family photos12Individuals, then pairs checkPlay the audio 2 times, not 3
6:32–6:45Grammar Q&A: Who's this? Do you have kids? 's + pair drill13Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; it becomes homework

7:00–7:10Talk Time: My family tree (own family or picture-card family)10Groups of 3 / groups of 3 (or 2 pairs)Each person says 2 sentences, not 3

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the third play of the audio; (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) the questions in Talk Time. Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. Print for the number you expect, plus 3 spares. Late arrivals join any pair or group right away. With 7–8 learners, Talk Time groups can be 2 groups of 3 + 1 pair, or 2 groups of 4.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Hello + Review · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
  • Before class: write on the board: What's your phone number? What's your address? What's his / her name?
  • Model with one learner: "What's your phone number?" → "555-0163." "Can you repeat, please?" Then point to another learner: "What's her name?" → "Her name is Rosa."
  • Do: pairs use the Hello + Review page. Practice numbers (555-01__) are fine. Then they ask about a classmate (What's his name? Where is she from?). Switch. Then find a new partner.
  • Homework check (last 3 min): partners show each other their Lesson 3 homework. Walk around and look at item 2 (my / his / her / our / their).
  • New learners: pair them with a strong partner. They can do the Lesson 1–3 Progress Checks at home.
  • If behind: one partner only.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:20 · New Words · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Say first: "Today: family. You can talk about your family or Ana's family." Point to the picture-card family page.
  • Show: draw a simple family tree on the board (stick figures are fine), or show one photo of a family. Point and say: "This is the mother. This is the father. They are the parents."
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat twice. The person with the blue circle is the word. For husband / wife, point to the ring.
  • kids = children: write kids = children on the board. "Kids" is everyday English. Also write 1 child → 2 children.
  • Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then switch. Then A says a word, B points.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:20–6:32 · Listening · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "This is Carlos. This is Kim. Carlos has photos of his family on his phone." Hold up your phone and pretend to show photos: "This is my wife… This is my son…"
  • Listen 1 → Task A: learners point to each person they hear, then write 1, 2, 3, 4 under the pictures in the order they hear them.
  • Listen 2 → Task B: learners write the names on Carlos's family tree (the names are in the box).
  • Listen 3 → Task C: learners write the numbers (how many children, ages).
  • Pairs compare after each task: "Show your partner." Then write the answers on the board.
  • The audio plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen.
  • If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.

Step 4 · 6:32–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 13 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer. Point left, then right.
  • Box 1: point to the picture-card family. "Who's this?" → "This is my mother. Her name is Lucia." A man → his. A woman → her. (The same as Lesson 3.)
  • Box 2 (the key point): "Do you have kids?" Nod: "Yes, I do." Shake your head: "No, I don't." Write on the board: Yes, I do. ✓ / Yes, I have. ✗. Then add the number: "Yes, I do. I have two."
  • Box 3: hold up a learner's pen: "This is Maria's pen." Then: "Ana's husband" = the husband of Ana. Say Carlos's = "CAR-los-iz".
  • Box 4: one son → two sons. Clap on the -s. Point to children and babies: these are different.
  • Check questions: "Do you have kids?" (Yes, I do. / No, I don't.) • point to a boy in a picture: "___ name is Daniel." (His) • "Ana has a husband. He's ___ husband." (Ana's)
  • Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks from the left side about the picture-card family (Who's this? How old is he?); B answers from the right side. Then switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. It becomes homework, and Talk Time practices the same questions.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: This is my ___. His / Her name is ___. He's / She's ___. and Who's this? How old is he / she? Do you have kids?
  • Draw the blank family tree on the board.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:10 · Talk Time: My Family Tree · 10 min

  • Grouping: groups of 3. 15 learners: 5 groups. 7–8 learners: 2 groups of 3 + 1 pair (or 2 groups of 4).
  • Say again: "Your family or Ana's family. You choose." Don't ask who chooses what.
  • Model (2 min): fill in the board tree with your family or an invented family. Say 3 sentences: "This is my sister. Her name is Laura. She's 30." Then a learner asks you one question: "How old is he?"
  • Part 1 (3 min): each learner fills in the blank tree with names (and ages if they want), or uses the picture-card family page. Learners who can't write yet can draw faces or point to the pictures.
  • Part 2 (5 min): in the group, each person shows the tree and says 3 sentences. The others ask one question each (Who's this? How old is he? Do you have kids?).
  • Fast groups: they say one sentence about a partner's family with 's: "Rosa's son is 12."
  • If behind: each person says 2 sentences, and skip the questions.

Step 6 · 7:10–7:15 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner says one sentence about a family member (or a person in Ana's family): "This is my son. His name is…" or writes Yes, I do. / No, I don't. for "Do you have kids?". Copying is fine.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (the first sentence). Point to each instruction so learners know what to do at home.

Letters & Numbers · 7:15–7:25 · Short Vowels, Plural -s, This / Is / My · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page.
  • See it (1 min): point to the 4 columns in Task A: a (dad), o (mom), u sound (son), i (kids).
  • Say it (3 min): say each column, top to bottom. Learners repeat. The vowels are short: say them quickly. Point out: son and mother are spelled with o, but sound like u in but.
  • Quick check (1 min): say dad or kids… Learners point to the column.
  • Write it (4 min): Task B: say the 5 words in the answer key, 2 times each. Learners circle. Task C: one → two: learners add -s. Show child → children (no -s). Task D: learners copy the 2 sentences. Point to the capital T and the period.
  • Partners: A points to a word in Task A, B reads it. Switch.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they say the words with everyone and point. In Task D they copy one sentence. A helper, if you have one, sits with them.
  • If behind: do Tasks A and B only.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 5 words (answer key), slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle.
  • Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 5). Part C shows who still mixes up his and her.
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 5 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L1_L4_listening.mp3 (about 1:15; the conversation plays once, so play the audio again if needed)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Hold up your phone at "Look."

Narrator: Lesson four. Listening. Carlos and Kim are at English class. Carlos has photos of his family on his phone. Listen.

Kim: Carlos, are those photos of your family?

Carlos: Yes, they are. Look. This is my wife. Her name is Elena.

Kim: Oh, nice. And who's this?

Carlos: This is my son. His name is Daniel. He's ten.

Kim: And this girl? Is she your daughter?

Carlos: Yes, she is. This is my daughter, Sofia. She's six.

Kim: Oh, and who's this? A baby!

Carlos: That's our baby, Leo. He's one.

Kim: So you have three children!

Carlos: Yes, I do. I have three kids. And these are my parents, Carmen and Pedro.

Kim: Your parents are here, too?

Carlos: No. They're in Colombia. What about you, Kim? Do you have kids?

Kim: No, I don't. But I have two brothers.

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A (order you hear): a son 2, b baby 4, c wife 1, d daughter 3.
  • Listening Task B (Carlos's family tree): mother Carmen, father Pedro, wife Elena, son Daniel, daughter Sofia, baby Leo.
  • Listening Task C: 1 3 (three children), 2 10, 3 6, 4 0 (Kim: "No, I don't."), 5 2 (two brothers).
  • Grammar practice: 1 do, 2 don't, 3 Her, 4 His, 5 Carlos's.
  • Homework 2 (do / don't): 1 do, 2 don't, 3 do, 4 don't.
  • Homework 3 ('s): 1 Carlos's son, 2 Kim's brothers, 3 Rosa's daughter.
  • Letters & Numbers Task B (the teacher says): 1 mom, 2 dad, 3 kids, 4 his, 5 big. Say each word 2 times.
  • Letters & Numbers Task C: brothers, sisters, sons, daughters, parents (and child → children).
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says): 1 father, 2 daughter, 3 wife, 4 brother, 5 grandmother. Say each word 2 times.
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 c, 2 d, 3 a, 4 b.
  • Progress Check Part C: 1 Her, 2 His, 3 Ana's.
  • Progress Check scoring: Part A /5 + Part B /4 + Part C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. Part A shows the family words; Part C shows his / her and 's.

Teacher notes

  • Sensitive topic: always offer the picture-card family. Never ask "Where is your husband?" or "Why don't you have kids?" Accept No, I don't and move on. Married / single is optional (one Q&A line on the Grammar page): don't ask it to a learner in front of the class.
  • The big mistake this week: Yes, I have. Spanish answers Sí, tengo. In English the short answer uses do: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. Then learners can add the number: I have two. Correct by nodding and saying "Yes, I do."
  • his / her again: many learners say my sister… his name. Point to the person in the picture: "A woman… her." Learners can read the Spanish note on their Grammar page; you don't need to explain it.
  • 's: Ana's husband (not the husband of Ana). Names that end in s add 's too: Carlos's ("CAR-los-iz").
  • parents is not "relatives": parents = mother and father only. For "all my family" say my family (or my relatives, for strong learners).
  • Plurals: most words add -s (brothers); child → children and baby → babies are different. Kids is common and easy: use it.
  • Ages: learners don't have to say their own age or their family's ages. Ana's family has ages for practice.
  • Mixed levels: strong learners add 's and a question (How old is Rosa's son?). New learners use only This is my ___. and point.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they take part fully in the speaking. On the tree they can draw faces instead of names. Don't make them read aloud.
  • Looking ahead: Lesson 5 (jobs) uses do again (Do you work at night?) and I don't…, and previews Does he / she…?.

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. The student pages have a Spanish line and a "My language" line for every task. Learners read those on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Listen or write?"), then go. Say less, show more. Use the same short words every time: Listen. Repeat. Point. Circle. Write. Partner. Group.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the instruction and the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Everyone has an answer. Some learners don't work now, work at home, or are students. Teach these answers on the first day of the topic: I'm a student. I'm a homemaker. I don't work now. Learners can also say a job they want or a job they had. Never ask where someone works if they don't offer it, and never ask about pay or work papers.

Lesson 5 (Week 5): What's Your Job?

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • say a job with a / an (I'm a cook. I'm an office worker.), or I'm a student / I'm a homemaker / I don't work now
  • ask and answer What do you do? and Where do you work? I work at a restaurant.
  • ask and answer Do you work at night / on weekends? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
  • say I don't work…
  • understand (not produce) the preview Does she work? Yes, she does.
  • choose a or an, say the sh sound, and read two job signs (Letters & Numbers block)

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 5 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • job picture cards: cut out one copy of the New Words page (one set for each group of 3–4), or point to the page
  • mini whiteboards or scrap paper for Letters & Numbers
  • phone + small speaker, L1_L5_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 30 min (cutting the cards takes 10).

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ cook • ★ cleaner (housekeeper) • ★ construction worker • ★ cashier • ★ driver • ★ mechanic • ★ server • nurse • painter • ★ factory • ★ office • ★ restaurant • student • homemaker

Review from Lessons 1–4

Do you have kids? Yes, I do. / No, I don't. • This is my wife. Her name is… • Where are you from? • What's your phone number?

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take the time from Grammar or Talk Time. The last 15 minutes are the Letters & Numbers block.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
6:00–6:10Hello + Review (Lesson 4 family questions) + homework check10Pairs, then new pairsOne partner only
6:10–6:20New Words (picture page) + pair picture game10Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:20–6:32Listening (audio): two neighbors talk about their jobs12Individuals, then pairs checkPlay the audio 2 times, not 3
6:32–6:45Grammar Q&A: What do you do? Where do you work? Do you work…? + preview + pair drill13Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; it becomes homework
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:10Talk Time: job guessing game + Find Someone Who10Groups of 3–4, then mingle / groups of 3–4, then mingleDo only the guessing game
7:10–7:15Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:15–7:25Letters & Numbers: a / an, the sh sound, job signs10Whole class, then pairsDo Tasks A and B only
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it in Week 6 at 6:00, while people arrive

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the third play of the audio; (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) Find Someone Who. Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. Print for the number you expect, plus 3 spares. Late arrivals join any pair or group right away. With 7–8 learners, the mingle works the same way: each learner talks to everyone.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Hello + Review · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
  • Before class: write on the board: Do you have kids? Do you have brothers or sisters? Who's this?
  • Model with one learner: "Do you have brothers or sisters?" → "Yes, I do. I have two brothers." Then show the picture-card family from Lesson 4 (or the board tree): "Who's this?" → "This is my mother."
  • Do: pairs use the Hello + Review page. Learners can use their family or Ana's family. Switch. Then find a new partner.
  • Homework check (last 3 min): partners show each other their Lesson 4 homework. Walk around and look at item 2 (do / don't).
  • New learners: pair them with a strong partner. They can do the Lesson 1–4 Progress Checks at home.
  • If behind: one partner only.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:20 · New Words · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Say first: "Today: jobs. What do you do? You can say: I'm a student. I'm a homemaker. I don't work now." Write these 3 answers on the board and leave them there.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat twice. Act out each job (cook: stir a pot; cleaner: sweep; driver: turn a wheel; cashier: scan and count money). Learners copy the action.
  • Places: factory, office, restaurant are places. Say: "A cook works at a restaurant."
  • Pairs (4 min): A acts out a job, B says it. Then switch. Then A points to a picture, B says it.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:20–6:32 · Listening · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "This is Rosa. This is Marco. They are neighbors." Point to two houses on the board, side by side. "They talk about their jobs."
  • Listen 1 → Task A: learners match each person to a job picture (write the letter).
  • Listen 2 → Task B: learners circle Yes or No.
  • Listen 3 → Task C: learners write do, don't, or does.
  • Pairs compare after each task: "Show your partner." Then write the answers on the board.
  • The preview line: after Task C, play the end again or read it: "Does your wife work, too? Yes, she does. She's a nurse." Say: "Does = a question about he or she. Level 2 practices it. Today: only listen."
  • The audio plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen.
  • If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.

Step 4 · 6:32–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 13 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer. Point left, then right.
  • Box 1 (the key point): "What do you do?" → "I'm a cook." Write on the board: a cook, a driver / an office worker. Say: before a, e, i, o, u → an. Point to the 3 "everyone" answers.
  • Box 2: "Where do you work?" → "I work at a restaurant." Point to the place pictures.
  • Box 3: "Do you work at night?" Nod: "Yes, I do." Shake: "No, I don't." (The same as Do you have kids? in Lesson 4.)
  • Box 4: "I work at night. I don't work in the morning." Use the board: ✓ work / ✗ don't work.
  • Preview box (1–2 min, no practice needed): read it once; the class repeats once. "Level 2. Only listen today."
  • Check questions: "I'm ___ cook." (a) • "I'm ___ office worker." (an) • "Do you work on weekends?" (Yes, I do. / No, I don't.)
  • Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks from the left side; B answers from the right side about a picture card (or about themselves). Then switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. It becomes homework, and Talk Time practices the same questions.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Cut or stack the job picture cards (one set per group). Write on the board: Are you a cook? Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. and Do you work at night? Do you work on weekends?

Step 5 · 7:00–7:10 · Talk Time: Job Guessing Game + Find Someone Who · 10 min

  • Part 1, guessing game (4 min): groups of 3–4. One learner takes a card (don't show it) and acts out the job. The others ask: "Are you a cook?" → "No, I'm not." / "Yes, I am!" The winner takes the next card. Model it first: you act out "driver"; the class guesses.
  • Part 2, Find Someone Who (6 min): everyone stands with the Talk Time page. Learners ask the questions and write a name when someone says Yes, I do (or No, I don't for the last line). One name per line; a different person for each line if possible.
  • Model Part 2: "Do you work at night?" → "No, I don't." → ask someone else → "Yes, I do." → write that name.
  • Finish: 2–3 learners report one line: "Ana works at night." (This is a preview of works; accept "Ana work at night" too.)
  • If behind: do only the guessing game.

Step 6 · 7:10–7:15 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner says one sentence about work: "I'm a cook." / "I work at a factory." / "I'm a student." / "I don't work now." or writes a or an for two words on the board (___ cook, ___ office worker).
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (the first sentence). Point to each instruction so learners know what to do at home.

Letters & Numbers · 7:15–7:25 · A / An, the Sh Sound, Job Signs · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page.
  • See it (2 min): Task A. Point to the vowel letters a e i o u. Read the a column, then the an column. Learners repeat. An goes before a vowel sound: an office, an apartment.
  • Write it (2 min): Task B. Learners write a or an. Check on the board.
  • Say it (2 min): Task C. Say sh like "Quiet!" (finger on lips). Then: she, shoe, cashier, English, wash. Learners repeat each word twice. Spanish speakers often say ch (as in chair): show the difference with a long, soft shhh.
  • Read it (3 min): Task D. Point to each sign and read it. Learners circle Yes or No. Ask: "Where do you see this sign?" (a store window; a door at work).
  • Partners: A says a job, B says a or an + the job. Switch.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they say the words with everyone and point. In Task D, read the signs aloud for them and let them answer by pointing.

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 5 words (answer key), slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle.
  • Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 6). Part C shows a / an and do / don't.
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 6 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L1_L5_listening.mp3 (about 1:10; the conversation plays once, so play the audio again if needed)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer.

Narrator: Lesson five. Listening. Rosa and Marco are neighbors. They talk about their jobs. Listen.

Rosa: Good morning, Marco!

Marco: Hi, Rosa. How are you?

Rosa: I'm fine, thanks. Marco, what do you do?

Marco: I'm a cook. I work at a restaurant on Main Street.

Rosa: Do you work at night?

Marco: Yes, I do. I don't work in the morning. And you? What do you do?

Rosa: I'm a cashier. I work at a store.

Marco: Do you work on weekends?

Rosa: Yes, I do. I work on Saturday and Sunday.

Marco: Oh, that's a lot of work!

Rosa: Yes, it is. Does your wife work, too?

Marco: Yes, she does. She's a nurse.

Rosa: Nice. My husband is a mechanic.

Marco: Great! OK, see you later, Rosa.

Rosa: Bye, Marco!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: 1 Rosa b (cashier), 2 Marco a (cook), 3 Marco's wife d (nurse), 4 Rosa's husband c (mechanic).
  • Listening Task B: 1 Yes, 2 Yes, 3 No (he doesn't work in the morning), 4 No (at a store), 5 Yes.
  • Listening Task C: 1 do, 2 don't, 3 do, 4 does (preview).
  • Grammar practice: 1 a, 2 an, 3 at, 4 do, 5 don't.
  • Homework 2 (a / an): 1 a, 2 an, 3 a, 4 an, 5 a.
  • Homework 3 (do / don't): answers can be do or don't, if they match the learner's Yes / No.
  • Letters & Numbers Task B: 1 a, 2 an, 3 a, 4 an, 5 a, 6 an.
  • Letters & Numbers Task D: 1 Yes, 2 No, 3 No, 4 Yes.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says): 1 cashier, 2 mechanic, 3 nurse, 4 factory, 5 server. Say each word 2 times.
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 c, 2 a, 3 d, 4 b.
  • Progress Check Part C: 1 a, 2 an, 3 don't.
  • Progress Check scoring: Part A /5 + Part B /4 + Part C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. Part A shows the job words; Part C shows a / an and don't.

Teacher notes

  • Respect: I'm a student, I'm a homemaker and I don't work now are full, correct answers. Learners can also say a job they want ("I want to be a nurse" is too hard for now; accept "Nurse!" with a smile). Never ask about pay, hours in detail, bosses, or work papers.
  • The big mistake this week: I'm cook. Spanish says Soy cocinero with no article. In English a job needs a / an: I'm a cook. Correct by holding up one finger: "a cook."
  • Questions need do: Where do you work? (not Where you work?). It is the same do as Do you have kids? in Lesson 4.
  • at for workplaces: I work at a restaurant / at a factory / at home. (in an office is also fine; don't correct it.)
  • The Does he / she…? preview: learners only hear and repeat it this week: Does your wife work? Yes, she does. She works at a hospital. Don't test it and don't explain the -s in works; Level 2 Lesson 1 teaches it. If a learner says She work at a hospital, just repeat it correctly: "Yes, she works at a hospital."
  • Jobs from home countries: many learners had a different job before. Accept "In Mexico, I'm a teacher" (past tense comes later).
  • Mixed levels: strong learners add a place and a time: I'm a cook. I work at a restaurant. I work at night. New learners use only I'm a ___. with a picture.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they play the guessing game fully and, in Find Someone Who, ask the questions while a partner writes names (or they draw a check).
  • Looking ahead: Lesson 6 (time and days) uses I work on Monday… at 6:00 and When do you work?.

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. The student pages have a Spanish line and a "My language" line for every task. Learners read those on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Listen or write?"), then go. Say less, show more. Use the same short words every time: Listen. Repeat. Point. Circle. Write. Partner. Group.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the instruction and the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Bring a clock you can move. A paper plate with two paper hands and a pin works well. (Any clock with hands works; a phone shows only numbers.) Teach :00 and :30 first, then :15 and :45.

Lesson 6 (Week 6): What Time Is It?

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • ask and tell the time: What time is it? It's six o'clock / six thirty / six fifteen / six forty-five.
  • say the days of the week, and the time and day of class: It's at 6:00. It's on Monday.
  • use at (a time), on (a day), in (the morning / the afternoon / the evening)
  • understand store hours: Is it open on Sunday? No, it isn't. It's closed. • It's open from 9:00 to 5:00.
  • say when they work: When do you work? On Monday and Tuesday, in the morning.
  • read and write times and short day names; read an OPEN sign (Letters & Numbers block)

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 6 (print for the number expected + 3 spares). Talk Time: print the Student A page for half the class and the Student B page for the other half.
  • a clock with hands you can move (a paper-plate clock is fine)
  • mini whiteboards or scrap paper for Letters & Numbers
  • phone + small speaker, L1_L6_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 30 min (15 if you already have a clock).

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ clock • ★ o'clock • ★ thirty (half past) • ★ morning • ★ afternoon • ★ evening / night • ★ day • ★ week • ★ weekend • ★ open • ★ closed • days of the week (Monday–Sunday)

Review from Lessons 1–5

What do you do? I'm a cook. • Where do you work? I work at a restaurant. • Do you work at night? Yes, I do. / No, I don't. • numbers 1–60

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take the time from Grammar or Talk Time. The last 15 minutes are the Letters & Numbers block.

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
