6:10–6:20New Words (picture page) + the class clock10Whole class, then pairsTeach :00 and :30 only
6:20–6:32Listening (audio): a store message and a call to a school12Individuals, then pairs checkPlay the audio 2 times, not 3
6:32–6:45Grammar Q&A: What time is it? at / on / in, Is it open…? + pair drill13Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; it becomes homework
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:10Talk Time: schedule information gap (A–B), then When do you work?10A–B pairs / A–B pairsSkip Part 2
7:10–7:15Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:15–7:25Letters & Numbers: times, days, short forms, a store-hours sign10Whole class, then pairsDo Tasks A and B only
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it in Week 7 at 6:00, while people arrive

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the third play of the audio; (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) Talk Time Part 2. Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. Print for the number you expect, plus 3 spares. Late arrivals join any pair right away. In Talk Time, an A always works with a B; with an odd number, two Bs share one A.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Hello + Review · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
  • Before class: write on the board: What do you do? Where do you work? Do you work at night? and the 3 "everyone" answers: I'm a student. I'm a homemaker. I don't work now.
  • Model with one learner: "What do you do?" → "I'm a cashier." "Where do you work?" → "I work at a store."
  • Do: pairs use the Hello + Review page. Switch. Then find a new partner.
  • Homework check (last 3 min): partners show each other their Lesson 5 homework. Walk around and look at item 2 (a / an).
  • New learners: pair them with a strong partner. They can do the Lesson 1–5 Progress Checks at home.
  • If behind: one partner only.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:20 · New Words · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show the class clock: set it to 9:00. "What time is it? It's nine o'clock." Move to 9:30: "It's nine thirty." Write both on the board: 9:00 = nine o'clock, 9:30 = nine thirty = half past nine.
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat twice. For morning / afternoon / evening, point to the sun moving (low, high, gone) with your arm.
  • Days: say Monday–Sunday. Learners repeat. Then: "Week = 7 days. Weekend = Saturday and Sunday."
  • Pairs (4 min): A sets a time on the class clock (or draws hands on paper), B says it. Then A points to a picture, B says the word.
  • If behind: teach :00 and :30 only.

Step 3 · 6:20–6:32 · Listening · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "Kim calls a laundromat." Mime washing clothes. "She hears a message. Then she calls a school." Hold up your phone.
  • Listen 1 → Task A: learners circle the times.
  • Listen 2 → Task B: learners check the days.
  • Listen 3 → Task C: learners write the times and the word.
  • Pairs compare after each task: "Show your partner." Then write the answers on the board.
  • The audio plays the message and the call once. Press play again for the next listen.
  • If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.

Step 4 · 6:32–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 13 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer. Point left, then right.
  • Box 1: move the class clock: 6:00, 6:30, 6:15, 6:45. The class answers "It's…" each time.
  • Boxes 2 and 4 (the key point): draw 3 boxes on the board: at 6:00 (a clock), on Monday (a calendar), in the morning (a sun). Say: "at + time. on + day. in + the morning." Exception to say once: at night.
  • Box 3: "When do you work?" → "On Monday and Tuesday." "In the morning." Learners who don't work: "When is English class?" → "On Monday, at 6:00."
  • Box 5: point to a store picture: "Is the store open on Sunday?" → "No, it isn't. It's closed." "What time is it open?" → "From 9:00 to 5:00."
  • Check questions: "Class is ___ 6:00." (at) • "Class is ___ Monday." (on) • "I work ___ the morning." (in)
  • Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks from the left side; B answers from the right side. Then switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. It becomes homework, and Talk Time practices the same questions.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Put the Student A and Student B pages in two piles. Write on the board: Is the ___ open on ___? What time is it open? From ___ to ___.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:10 · Talk Time: Schedule Information Gap · 10 min

  • Grouping: A–B pairs. Give half the class the Student A page and half the Student B page. Partners don't show their pages.
  • Model with one learner (you are A): "Is the library open on Monday?" → "No, it isn't." "Is it open on Tuesday?" → "Yes, it is." "What time is it open?" → "From 10:00 to 6:00." Write it in the empty table on the board.
  • Part 1 (6 min): A asks about B's 3 places and writes the days and times. Then B asks about A's places.
  • Check (1 min): partners show their pages and compare.
  • Part 2 (3 min): new question: "When do you work?" (or "When do you study? When is English class?"). Each learner says one sentence: "I work on Monday and Friday, in the morning." / "I don't work now. English class is on ___, at 6:00."
  • If behind: skip Part 2.

Step 6 · 7:10–7:15 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: set the class clock to a time. Each learner says the time ("It's seven fifteen.") or writes one sentence: Class is on ___, at ___. Copying is fine.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (the first line). Point to each instruction so learners know what to do at home.

Letters & Numbers · 7:15–7:25 · Times, Days, Short Forms, a Store Sign · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page.
  • See it (2 min): Task A: point to each clock and the time under it. Say: six o'clock, six fifteen, six thirty, six forty-five. Learners repeat. Show the : (two dots) between the hour and the minutes.
  • Write it (3 min): Task B: say the 4 times in the answer key, 2 times each. Learners write them with numbers (7:30).
  • Days (2 min): Task C: days start with a capital letter. The short form is 3 letters + a period: Mon. Learners write the short forms.
  • Read it (2 min): Task D: read the sign together. Say: "AM = morning. PM = afternoon and night." Learners circle Yes / No and write the time.
  • Partners: A says a time, B writes it. Switch.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they say the times with everyone and point to the clocks. In Task C they copy Mon. and Sat. only. A helper, if you have one, sits with them.
  • If behind: do Tasks A and B only.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 5 times (answer key), slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle.
  • Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
  • Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 7). Part C shows at / on / in.
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 7 at 6:00, while learners arrive.

Listening script: L1_L6_listening.mp3 (about 1:00; the message and the call play once, so play the audio again if needed)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer (one person reads the message and the receptionist; the other reads Kim).

Narrator: Lesson six. Listening. Part one. Kim calls a laundromat. She hears a message. Listen.

Message: Thank you for calling City Laundromat. We are open Monday to Saturday, from seven in the morning to nine at night. We are closed on Sunday. Thank you.

Narrator: Part two. Kim calls the adult school. Listen.

Receptionist: Good afternoon. Riverside Adult School.

Kim: Hi. What time is the English class?

Receptionist: It's at six o'clock.

Kim: Six o'clock. OK. What day is the class?

Receptionist: It's on Monday and Wednesday.

Kim: Is the school open on Friday?

Receptionist: Yes, it is. It's open from nine to three. It's closed on the weekend.

Kim: OK. Thank you!

Receptionist: You're welcome. Bye!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: 1 7:00, 2 9:00, 3 6:00.
  • Listening Task B: laundromat: ✓ Mon., Tue., Wed., Thu., Fri., Sat. (not Sun.) • English class: ✓ Mon., ✓ Wed.
  • Listening Task C: 1 9:00 to 3:00, 2 weekend.
  • Grammar practice: 1 at, 2 on, 3 in, 4 at, 5 on.
  • Talk Time (both pages): Clinic Mon.–Fri. 8:00–5:00 • Store every day 7:00–10:00 • Laundromat Mon.–Sat. 6:00–9:00 • Library Tue.–Sat. 10:00–6:00 • Restaurant every day 11:00–9:00 • Bank Mon.–Fri. 9:00–4:00.
  • Homework 2 (at / on / in): 1 on, 2 at, 3 in, 4 on, 5 at.
  • Homework 3: 1 7:00, 2 8:30, 3 4:15, 4 5:45.
  • Letters & Numbers Task B (the teacher says): 1 7:30, 2 8:00, 3 9:15, 4 10:45. Say each time 2 times.
  • Letters & Numbers Task C: Mon., Tue., Wed., Thu., Fri., Sat., Sun.
  • Letters & Numbers Task D: 1 Yes, 2 No, 3 9:00 (9 AM) to 5:00 (5 PM).
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says): 1 6:30, 2 7:15, 3 3:00, 4 9:45, 5 11:30. Say each time 2 times.
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 c, 2 a, 3 d, 4 b.
  • Progress Check Part C: 1 at, 2 on, 3 in.
  • Progress Check scoring: Part A /5 + Part B /4 + Part C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. Part A shows who can hear times; Part C shows at / on / in.

Teacher notes

  • The big mistake this week: They are six. Spanish says Son las seis. In English: It's six o'clock (never They are). Correct by tapping the clock: "It's six."
  • at / on / in: Spanish uses a las 6 and el lunes. In English: at 6:00, on Monday (not the Monday), in the morning, but at night. Learners can read the Spanish note on their Grammar page.
  • Times: teach :00 and :30 first. :15 and :45 are said as numbers (six fifteen, six forty-five). Quarter past / quarter to is Level 2; accept it if a learner knows it.
  • -teen / -ty again: 7:15 and 7:50 sound alike. Say "fif-TEEN" and "FIF-ty" with a clap, as in Lesson 3.
  • AM / PM: say once: AM = morning, PM = afternoon and night. Signs use them; learners don't need to say them.
  • Days: days always start with a capital letter: Monday. Short forms: Mon., Tue., Wed., Thu., Fri., Sat., Sun.
  • Work schedules: don't ask about real hours if a learner doesn't offer them. English class is on Monday at 6:00 is always a good answer.
  • Mixed levels: strong learners add from… to… (I work from 8:00 to 4:00). New learners use only It's ___. with the clock.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they set the class clock and say times. In Talk Time, they ask the questions while a partner writes, or they point to the days.
  • Looking ahead: Lesson 7 (money and clothes) uses numbers again for prices (It's $12) and this / these.

Q: is or are?

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. The student pages have a Spanish line and a "My language" line for every task. Learners read those on their own. You never need to read, translate, or explain them.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Listen or write?"), then go. Say less, show more. Use the same short words every time: Listen. Repeat. Point. Circle. Write. Partner. Group.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck or speaks another language to you: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the instruction and the grammar box on their page; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English. You don't need to understand what classmates say to each other.

Money is private. Use only play money and the invented prices on the pages. Never ask what learners earn, spend, or pay for rent, and never ask them to show real money or real cards.

Lesson 7 (Week 7): How Much Is It?

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • ask the price: How much is this shirt? How much are these shoes?
  • understand and say prices: It's $12. They're $30. It's $4.99 ("four ninety-nine").
  • use this / that (one) and these / those (two or more)
  • name clothes and colors, with the color before the noun: a blue shirt, black shoes
  • pay and check the change: Cash or credit card? Cash, please. Here's $20. Your change is $5.
  • read prices and a simple receipt (Letters & Numbers block)

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 7 (print for the number expected + 3 spares). Talk Time: print the Student A page for half the class and the Student B page for the other half.
  • play money: print the play-money page (one per pair is enough) and cut it before class. Put each pair's money in an envelope.
  • 2 or 3 real clothes you can hold up (a shirt or a jacket, a pair of shoes), and one far away on a chair (for that / those)
  • mini whiteboards or scrap paper for Letters & Numbers
  • phone + small speaker, L1_L7_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 40 min (printing and cutting the play money).

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ dollar • ★ cent • coin • ★ cash • ★ credit card • receipt • ★ shirt • ★ pants • ★ shoes • ★ jacket • ★ dress • colors (red, blue, black, white, green, yellow)

Review from Lessons 1–6

What time is it? It's 6:30. • at 6:00, on Monday, in the morning • Is the store open on Sunday? • numbers 1–100

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take the time from Grammar or Talk Time. The last 15 minutes are the Letters & Numbers block.

6:32–6:45Grammar Q&A: How much is / are…? this / that / these / those, color + noun + pair drill13Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; it becomes homework

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the third play of the audio; (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) Talk Time Part 2. Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. Print for the number you expect, plus 3 spares. Late arrivals join any pair right away. In Talk Time, an A always works with a B; with an odd number, two Bs share one A (one is the shopper, one helps count the money).

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Hello + Review · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
  • Before class: write on the board: What time is it? What time is class? What day is class? Is the store open on Sunday?
  • Model with one learner: "What time is it?" → "It's six o'clock." "What day is class?" → "It's on Monday."
  • Do: pairs use the Hello + Review page. Switch. Then find a new partner.
  • Homework check (last 3 min): partners show each other their Lesson 6 homework. Walk around and look at item 2 (at / on / in).
  • New learners: pair them with a strong partner. They can do the Lesson 1–6 Progress Checks at home.
  • If behind: one partner only.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:20 · New Words · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: hold up a real shirt: "This is a shirt. It's blue." Hold up shoes: "Shoes. Two shoes." Point to colors in the room: "Red. Black. White."
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat twice. For cash, show the play money; for credit card, mime paying with a card. 100 cents = 1 dollar (write it on the board).
  • pants, shoes: say "pants" and hold up 2 fingers: one item, but the word is always plural.
  • Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then A says a color, B points to something in the room with that color.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:20–6:32 · Listening · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "Ana is at a clothing store. She asks: How much is it?" Point to the shirts and shoes in Task A.
  • Listen 1 → Task A: learners circle the color of the shirt and the shoes Ana buys.
  • Listen 2 → Task B: learners write the 2 prices.
  • Listen 3 → Task C: learners check the total, cash or card, and write the change.
  • Pairs compare after each task: "Show your partner." Then write the answers on the board.
  • The audio plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen.
  • If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.

Step 4 · 6:32–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 13 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer. Point left, then right.
  • Boxes 1–2: hold up the shirt: "How much is this shirt?" → "It's $12." Hold up the shoes: "How much are these shoes?" → "They're $30." Write on the board: one → is / it's. two or more → are / they're.
  • Box 3 (the key point): stand next to the shirt: "this shirt." Walk away and point to the far chair: "that shirt." Same with shoes: "these shoes… those shoes." Learners point near and far as they say the words.
  • Box 4: write a shirt blue on the board and cross it out with an ✗. Write a blue shirt ✓. Then black shoes ✓ and blacks shoes ✗: colors never take -s.
  • Box 5: model paying with play money: "That's $8." → give $10 → "Your change is $2."
  • Check questions: hold up one shirt: "How much ___ this shirt?" (is) • hold up shoes: "How much ___ these shoes?" (are) • "shirt / red / a" (a red shirt)
  • Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A points to a picture on the New Words page and asks; B invents a price. Then switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. It becomes homework, and Talk Time practices the same questions.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Put the Student A and Student B pages in two piles, and one envelope of play money per pair. Write on the board: How much is this ___? It's $___. How much are these ___? They're $___. Cash or credit card? Here's $___. Your change is $___.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:10 · Talk Time: Store Role Play · 10 min

  • Grouping: A–B pairs. Give half the class the Student A page and half the Student B page, and each pair one envelope of play money. Partners don't show their pages.
  • Model with one learner (you are the shopper): point to the dress on your page. "How much is this red dress?" → "It's $25." "OK. Here's $30." → "Your change is $5." Write the price and the change on the board.
  • Part 1 (4 min): A is the cashier (Store 1, with prices). B is the shopper: B gets the play money, asks the price of the 3 things, writes the prices, buys one thing, pays, and checks the change.
  • Part 2 (4 min): switch. B is the cashier (Store 2). A is the shopper.
  • Check (2 min): partners show their pages. Are the prices the same?
  • Fast pairs: buy 2 things and say the total: "That's $43."
  • If behind: one round only (Part 1).

Step 6 · 7:10–7:15 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: hold up a picture or a real item. Each learner asks "How much is this ___?" / "How much are these ___?" or writes one color + noun (a red dress). Copying is fine.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (the first line). Point to each instruction so learners know what to do at home.
  • Collect the play money for next time.

Letters & Numbers · 7:15–7:25 · Prices, This / These, a Receipt · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page.
  • See it (2 min): Task A: point to each price and say it. $4.99 = "four ninety-nine"; $12.50 = "twelve fifty"; $20.00 = "twenty dollars". The dot is a period; the numbers after it are cents.
  • Hear it (2 min): Task B: say the 5 prices in the answer key, 2 times each. Learners circle.
  • Say it (2 min): Task C: this has a short i (like six); these has a long ee (like three). Smile wide for ee. Say the pairs; learners repeat.
  • Read it (3 min): Task D: read the receipt together. Learners answer the 3 questions.
  • Partners: A says a price from Task A, B points to it. Switch.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: they say the prices with everyone and point. In Task D they find and circle the TOTAL. A helper, if you have one, sits with them.
  • If behind: do Tasks A and B only.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the 5 prices (answer key), slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle.
  • Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Walk around and help with the instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
  • Collect the pages. Week 8 is the midterm; Parts A and C show who needs a quick review of prices and is / are.
  • If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 8 at 6:00, before the midterm.

Listening script: L1_L7_listening.mp3 (about 1:10; the conversation plays once, so play the audio again if needed)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Say the prices as words: twelve dollars, thirty dollars.

Narrator: Lesson seven. Listening. Ana is at a clothing store. She talks to the cashier. Listen.

Cashier: Hi! Can I help you?

Ana: Yes, please. How much is this shirt?

Cashier: The blue shirt? It's $12.

Ana: Do you have this shirt in red?

Cashier: No, sorry. Only blue and white.

Ana: OK, blue is good. And how much are these shoes?

Cashier: The black shoes? They're $30.

Ana: Good. The blue shirt and the black shoes, please.

Cashier: OK. That's $42. Cash or credit card?

Ana: Cash, please. Here's $50.

Cashier: Thank you. Your change is $8.

Ana: Thank you. Can I have the receipt, please?

Cashier: Sure. Here's your receipt. Have a nice day!

Ana: You too. Bye!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

  • Listening Task A: the shirt: b (blue) • the shoes: a (black).
  • Listening Task B: 1 $12, 2 $30.
  • Listening Task C: 1 ✓ $42, 2 ✓ cash, 3 $8, 4 ✓ the receipt.
  • Grammar practice: 1 is, 2 are, 3 this, 4 these, 5 a red shirt.
  • Talk Time: Store 1: red dress $25, black pants $18, white shoes $35 • Store 2: green jacket $40, yellow shirt $9, blue pants $22.
  • Homework 1: 1 is, 2 are, 3 are, 4 is.
  • Homework 2: 1 a green jacket, 2 black shoes, 3 a white dress.
  • Letters & Numbers Task B (the teacher says): 1 $4.99 ("four ninety-nine"), 2 $13 ("thirteen dollars"), 3 $15.50 ("fifteen fifty"), 4 $60 ("sixty dollars"), 5 $2.25 ("two twenty-five"). Say each price 2 times.
  • Letters & Numbers Task D: 1 $40.00, 2 $83.00, 3 $17.00.
  • Progress Check Part A (the teacher says): 1 $12, 2 $40, 3 $5.99 ("five ninety-nine"), 4 $18, 5 $70. Say each price 2 times.
  • Progress Check Part B: 1 c, 2 a, 3 d, 4 b.
  • Progress Check Part C: 1 are, 2 is, 3 a red dress.
  • Progress Check scoring: Part A /5 + Part B /4 + Part C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. Part A shows who can hear prices (and -teen / -ty again); Part C shows is / are and color + noun.

Teacher notes

  • Money is private: only play money and invented prices. If a learner talks about real prices or real money problems, listen kindly and move back to the activity.
  • The big mistake this week: the color after the noun. Spanish says una camisa azul. In English the color comes first: a blue shirt. And colors never take -s: black shoes (not blacks shoes). Correct by pointing at the word order on the board. Learners can read the Spanish note on their Grammar page.
  • is / are: one thing → How much is this shirt? It's $12. Two or more → How much are these shoes? They're $30. Pants and shoes always use are.
  • this / that / these / those: near / far + one / more than one. Use your body: stand next to the thing for this / these, point far away for that / those.
  • Saying prices: $4.99 = "four ninety-nine" (people don't say the word dollars or cents here). $12 = "twelve dollars". $12.50 = "twelve fifty". -teen / -ty matter again: $13 or $30?
  • this and these: many learners say both the same. this = short i (sit); these = long ee (see). Don't over-correct; the grammar (is / are) helps listeners understand.
  • Mixed levels: strong learners buy 2 things, say the total, and use Do you have this in ___? New learners use only How much is this? and point.
  • Learners who can't read or write yet: in Talk Time they are good cashiers: they say the price from the tag and count the play money.
  • Looking ahead: Week 8 is the midterm (Lessons 1–7). Lesson 8 (food) uses How much is…? again and adds I like… / I don't like….

lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. The student pages have a Spanish line and a "My language" line for every task. Learners read those on their own.

Instruction rule: Model it (do it with one learner while everyone watches), check it (ask: "Listen or write?"), then go. Say less, show more. Use the same short words every time: Listen. Repeat. Point. Circle. Write. Partner. Group.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: turn to a neighbor; with an odd number, make one group of 3. Groups: 3–4 learners. Mingle: everyone stands and talks to many classmates. The teacher joins a pair only if one learner is left over.

When a learner is stuck: (1) show it: the picture, a gesture, or the board; (2) give one more short English example; (3) point to the instruction and the grammar box; (4) a classmate can help for a few seconds, then back to English.

Food tip: Ask about allergies and food rules without making anyone explain why. "I don't eat ___." is always an OK answer. Never ask how much learners spend on food.

Lesson 8 (Week 9): Let's Eat!

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • name common foods and drinks (breakfast, lunch, dinner, beans, tortillas, meat, fish, fruit, vegetables, juice, soda, pizza)
  • ask and answer Do you like…? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
  • say I like… / I don't like…
  • order: I want a taco and a soda. / A coffee, please.
  • answer For here or to go? and Anything else?
  • read a simple picture menu with prices (Real-World Reading)

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 8 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • food picture cards: cut one New Words page per group of 3–4, or point to the page
  • picture menu (on Talk Time and Real-World Reading pages)
  • mini whiteboards or scrap paper for Real-World Reading
  • phone + small speaker, L1_L8_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 30 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ breakfast • ★ lunch • ★ dinner • ★ beans • ★ tortillas • ★ meat • ★ fish • ★ fruit • ★ vegetables • ★ juice • soda • pizza

Review from Lessons 1–7

How much is this? It's $5. • Do you work on weekends? • What time is the class? • Cash or credit card? Midterm was Week 8.

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take the time from Grammar or Talk Time. The last 15 minutes are Real-World Reading (Weeks 9–14).

TimeStepMinGrouping (15 / 7–8)If running behind
6:00–6:10Hello + Review (prices + Do you…?) + homework check10Pairs, then new pairsOne partner only
6:10–6:20New Words (picture page) + pair picture game10Whole class, then pairsTeach the ★ words only
6:20–6:32Listening (audio): Ana orders at a taco truck12Individuals, then pairs checkPlay the audio 2 times, not 3
6:32–6:45Grammar Q&A: Do you like…? I want… For here or to go? + pair drill13Whole class, then pairsSkip the pair drill; it becomes homework
6:45–7:00BREAK15
7:00–7:10Talk Time: food survey + taco-truck role play (A/B)10Groups, then A–B pairsDo only the survey
7:10–7:15Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:15–7:25Real-World Reading: picture menu, for here / to go, store signs10Whole class, then pairsDo Tasks A and B only
7:25–7:30Progress Check5IndividualsDo it next week at 6:00

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the third play of the audio; (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time. Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. Print for the number you expect, plus 3 spares. Late arrivals join any pair or group right away.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Hello + Review · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
  • Before class: write on the board: How much is this shirt? Do you like coffee? Do you work on weekends?
  • Model with one learner: "Do you like coffee?" → "Yes, I do." / "No, I don't."
  • Do: pairs use the Hello + Review page. Switch. Then find a new partner.
  • Homework check (last 3 min): partners show Lesson 7 homework (prices). Walk around and look.
  • New learners: pair them with a strong partner. They can review Lesson 7 New Words at home.
  • If behind: one partner only.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:20 · New Words · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: hold up or draw a taco: "This is a taco. Tortillas. Beans." Mime eating: "Breakfast. Lunch. Dinner."
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat twice. ★ words twice more.
  • Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then A asks "Do you like ___?" and B answers Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
  • Spanish tip (on the page only): I like tacos (no the for things in general).
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:20–6:32 · Listening · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "Ana is at a taco truck. She asks: Do you like…? She wants food." Point to Task A pictures.
  • Listen 1 → Task A: circle what Ana orders.
  • Listen 2 → Task B: does the server like fish tacos? Circle 😀 or 😐.
  • Listen 3 → Task C: write the prices, cash, change, for here / to go.
  • Pairs compare after each task. Write answers on the board.
  • Say it: class repeats I want a fish taco and a soda, please. and For here or to go?
  • The audio plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen.
  • If behind: play 2 times; do Task C together.

Step 4 · 6:32–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 13 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: Grammar page. Left = question. Right = answer.
  • Boxes 1–2: "Do you like fish?" → "Yes, I do. / No, I don't." "I like tacos. I don't like coffee." Cross out Me like and I like the tacos (for things in general).
  • Box 3: "What do you want?" → "I want a taco." / "A coffee, please."
  • Box 4: mime the counter: "For here or to go?" → "To go, please." "Anything else?" → "No, thanks."
  • Check questions: "Do you ___ fish?" (like) • "I ___ a soda." (want) • "To go or ___ here?" (for)
  • Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks Do you like…? B answers; then A orders from the menu and B is the server.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices the same language.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Put Student A (server) and Student B (customer) pages in two piles. Write on the board: Do you like ___? I want ___. For here or to go? How much is it?

Step 5 · 7:00–7:10 · Talk Time: Food Survey + Taco Truck · 10 min

  • Grouping: groups of 3–4 for the survey; then A–B pairs for the truck. Partners don't show their role cards if you cut them apart.
  • Part 1 — Food survey (4 min): each learner asks 3 classmates Do you like…? and writes 😀 or 😐. Model: "Do you like fish?" → "Yes, I do." (write 😀).
  • Part 2 — Taco truck (5 min): A is the server (menu with prices). B is the customer: orders, says for here / to go, asks the price, pays. Then switch.
  • Model with one learner before Part 2.
  • If behind: survey only.

Step 6 · 7:10–7:15 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner says I like ___. or I want ___. or writes one sentence. Copying from the box is fine.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 line 1 together. Point to each instruction.

Real-World Reading · 7:15–7:25 · Picture Menu · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Use the Real-World Reading page (same menu as Talk Time).
  • See it (2 min): Task A — point to each food and the price. Say the prices as words.
  • Hear it (2 min): say 3 prices; learners point.
  • Read it (4 min): Tasks B–C — for here / to go; copy one menu line.
  • Partners: A is the server, B orders one thing from the menu (no money this time).
  • Learners who can't read yet: they point to pictures and say the food words with everyone.
  • If behind: Tasks A and B only.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals.
  • Part A: read the 3 words (answer key), slowly, 2 times. Learners circle.
  • Parts B and C: match and write. Help with instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line; learners check one face.
  • Collect if you want. After the midterm, these checks are light.
  • If behind: do it next week at 6:00.

Listening script: L1_L8_listening.mp3 (about 1:10; the conversation plays once, so play the audio again if needed)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Say the prices as words: three dollars, two dollars, five dollars, ten dollars.

Narrator: Lesson eight. Listening. Ana is at a taco truck. She talks to the server about food she likes. Listen.

Server: Hi! What do you want today?

Ana: Hi. Do you like the fish tacos?

Server: Yes, I do. They're really good.

Ana: Do you like the bean tacos, too?

Server: Yes, I do. A lot of people like them.

Ana: OK. I want a fish taco and a soda, please.

Server: For here or to go?

Ana: To go, please.

Server: Anything else? Juice or fruit?

Ana: No, thanks. How much is it?

Server: The taco is three dollars. The soda is two dollars. That's five dollars.

Ana: OK. Here's ten dollars.

Server: Thank you. Your change is five dollars. Have a nice day!

Ana: You too. Bye!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

Listening

  • A: fish taco, soda (not pizza, not juice)
  • B: 😀 likes
  • C: taco $3; soda $2; total $5; cash $10; change $5; to go

Grammar practice: 1 like 2 don't 3 want 4 to go 5 like 6 like or want (answers will vary)

Homework 2: 1 I like fruit. 2 I don't like coffee. 3 I want a taco.

Real-World Reading A: taco $3; juice $2; pizza slice $3; soda $1. B: 1 for here 2 to go 3 Anything else? C: answers will vary (copy from menu). D: partner practice (no written key).

Progress Check A (teacher reads twice each): 1 breakfast 2 fish 3 juice 4 beans 5 lunch B: 1–b 2–c 3–a 4–d C: answers vary (like / don't like / want) Scoring: A /5 + B /4 + C /3 = /12. Not a test grade.

Teacher notes

  • Invented prices and a fictional taco truck. No real restaurant names.
  • After the midterm (Week 8), keep energy light; this lesson recycles Do you…? and prices from Lesson 7.
  • Allergies: accept I don't eat ___ or I don't like ___ with no follow-up questions about why.
  • I'd like, some / any, and count vs non-count stay in Level 2.
  • Big mistake this week: Me like tacos and I like the tacos (for food in general). Point to Grammar Box 2.
  • Learners who can't write yet: they can point on the menu and say A taco, please / To go.
  • Talk Time odd number: two customers share one server, or one survey trio.

How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. The student pages have a Spanish line and a "My language" line for every task.

Instruction rule: Model it, check it, then go. Same short words: Listen. Repeat. Point. Circle. Write. Partner. Group.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: neighbor (odd → one group of 3). Groups: 3–4. Mingle: stand and talk to many classmates.

When a learner is stuck: show the picture or board → one short English example → point to the grammar box → classmate helps briefly, then English again.

Birthdays only — no holidays. Learners may use an invented birthday. Never ask about religious or cultural holidays.

Lesson 9 (Week 10): What's the Date?

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • say the months and write a date (May 5th / 5/5)
  • say When is your birthday? It's on May 5th. / It's in May.
  • understand an appointment day and time
  • ask How's the weather? → It's cold / hot / sunny / rainy.
  • use in (month), on (date or day), at (time)
  • read a simple appointment card (Real-World Reading)

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 9 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • picture cards from the New Words page (one set per group of 3–4)
  • appointment picture / cards for Talk Time
  • ordinals card (1st–5th…)
  • mini whiteboards or scrap paper for Real-World Reading
  • phone + small speaker, L1_L9_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 30 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ calendar • ★ month • ★ date • ★ birthday • ★ appointment • ★ today • ★ tomorrow • ★ sunny • ★ rainy • ★ cold • ★ hot • months (Jan–Dec)

Review

Do you like fish? What do you want for lunch? (Lesson 8)

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Hello + Review · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
  • Before class: write on the board: Do you like fish? What do you want for lunch? What day is today?
  • Model with one learner: "Do you like fish?" → "Yes, I do." Then "What day is today?"
  • Do: pairs use the Hello + Review page. Switch. Then find a new partner.
  • Homework check (last 3 min): partners show last week's homework. Walk around and look.
  • New learners: pair them with a strong partner.
  • If behind: one partner only.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:20 · New Words · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: point to a calendar: "Month. Date. Today. Tomorrow." Mime weather: "Sunny. Rainy. Cold. Hot." Show ordinals: "first, second, third…"
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat twice. ★ words twice more.
  • Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then A asks When is your birthday? (invented OK).
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:20–6:32 · Listening · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "Kim calls the clinic. She makes an appointment. Then Kim and Marco talk about the weather and birthdays."
  • Listen 1 → Task A. Listen 2 → Task B. Listen 3 → Task C.
  • Pairs compare after each task. Write answers on the board.
  • Say it: class repeats: Thursday, May tenth, at ten thirty. and How's the weather?
  • The audio plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen.
  • If behind: play 2 times; do Task C together.

Step 4 · 6:32–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 13 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: Grammar page. Left = question. Right = answer. Point left, then right.
  • Box 1: What's the date today? → It's October 20th.
  • Box 2: When is your birthday? → It's on May 5th. / It's in May. Board: on + date/day; in + month.
  • Box 3: When is your appointment? → On Tuesday at 3:00. (at + time)
  • Box 4: How's the weather? → It's sunny / rainy / cold / hot. Cross out It makes cold.
  • Check questions: "My birthday is ___ May." (in) • "My birthday is ___ May 5th." (on) • "Class is ___ 6:00." (at)
  • Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks birthday / appointment / weather; B answers; switch.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices the same language.

  • Grouping: whole class for the birthday line; then A–B pairs for the appointment.

  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 line 1 together. Point to each instruction.

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Use the Real-World Reading page.
  • See it (2 min): Task A — point to day, date, time on the appointment card.
  • Hear it (2 min): say 3 dates; learners point or write.

  • If behind: Tasks A and B only.

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the items in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle.
  • Parts B and C: match and write on their own. Help with instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line; learners check one face.
  • Collect if you want. These checks are light practice, not a test grade.
  • If behind: do it next week at 6:00.

Listening script: L1_L9_listening.mp3 (about 1:10; the conversation plays once, so play the audio again if needed)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Say dates as words: May tenth, May fifth, ten thirty.

Narrator: Lesson nine. Listening. Part one. Kim calls the clinic. She makes an appointment. Listen.

Receptionist: Good morning. Riverside Clinic.

Kim: Hi. I need an appointment, please.

Receptionist: OK. How about Thursday, May tenth, at ten thirty?

Kim: Thursday, May tenth, at ten thirty. Is that in the morning?

Receptionist: Yes, it is. Ten thirty in the morning.

Kim: OK. Thank you!

Receptionist: You're welcome. See you Thursday.

Narrator: Part two. Kim and Marco talk about the weather and birthdays. Listen.

Kim: Hi, Marco. How's the weather today?

Marco: It's sunny and hot. I like sunny days.

Kim: Me too. When is your birthday?

Marco: It's on May fifth. Next week!

Kim: Oh, soon! My birthday is in October.

Marco: Nice. See you later, Kim!

Kim: Bye, Marco!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

Listening A: Thursday; May 10; 10:30 (morning). B: sunny, hot. C: Marco — May 5th; Kim — October. Grammar practice: 1 on 2 in 3 at 4 sunny (or rainy / cold / hot) 5 on 6 answers will vary (today's date) Homework 2: 1 in 2 on 3 at 4 on Real-World Reading A: Thursday; May 10; 10:30. B: 5/10 → b May 10; 10/5 → a October 5; 12/25 → c December 25 C: answers will vary (today's date). D: partner practice (no written key). Progress Check A (teacher reads twice each): 1 May 2 sunny 3 10:30 4 cold 5 today B: 1–b 2–a 3–c 4–d C: 1 in 2 on 3 at 4 on Scoring: A /5 + B /4 + C /4 = /13. Not a test grade.

Teacher notes

  • Invented clinic (Riverside Clinic) and dates. U.S. date order: month/day/year.
  • No holidays. Never ask about religious or cultural holidays. Invented birthdays are fine.
  • Ordinals 1st–31st: teach with the card; Progress Check uses common ones.
  • Weather: It's cold (not It makes cold); I'm cold for people.
  • Big mistake this week: in May 5th / at May. Point to Grammar Box 2.
  • Learners who can't write yet: they say the month and point to the calendar.

Narrator: Lesson ten. Listening. Rosa calls about an apartment. She talks to the rental agent. Listen.

Agent: Hello. Green Street Apartments.

Rosa: Hi. Is there an apartment for rent?

Agent: Yes, there is. There are two bedrooms and one bathroom.

Rosa: Is there a washing machine?

Agent: No, there isn't. But there is a refrigerator in the kitchen.

Rosa: OK. Are there windows in the kitchen?

Agent: Yes, there are. There are two windows.

Rosa: How many bedrooms are there?

Agent: There are two bedrooms. The living room is big.

Rosa: Is the living room big?

Agent: Yes, it is. The living room is big.

Rosa: When is the rent due?

Agent: The rent is due on the first of the month.

Rosa: OK. Thank you. Goodbye.

Agent: Goodbye. Have a nice day!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Grammar practice: 1 is 2 are 3 Is 4 Are 5 are 6–7 answers will vary Homework 2: 1 is 2 are 3 is 4 are Real-World Reading A: 2; 1; $900. B: 2 BR → b bedrooms; 1 BA → a bathroom; /mo → c per month C: 1 Yes 2 Yes. D: partner practice (no written key). lessons.teacher:
How to Use This Plan

You don't need to speak Spanish or any other language. Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. The student pages have a Spanish line and a "My language" line for every task.

Instruction rule: Model it, check it, then go. Same short words: Listen. Repeat. Point. Circle. Write. Partner. Group.

Grouping toolkit: Pairs: neighbor (odd → one group of 3). Groups: 3–4. Mingle: stand and talk to many classmates.

When a learner is stuck: show the picture or board → one short English example → point to the grammar box → classmate helps briefly, then English again.

Invented streets only. Use the map on the page. Never send learners into a real street alone for homework.

Lesson 11 (Week 12): Around Town

At a glance

Objectives: learners can…

  • name places in town (bank, pharmacy, park, school…)
  • say Where's the…? It's next to / across from / between…
  • give and follow simple directions (Go straight. Turn left.)
  • understand a short directions dialogue
  • read a simple map and street signs

Materials

  • Student Pages for Lesson 11 (print for the number expected + 3 spares)
  • picture cards from the New Words page (one set per group of 3–4)
  • map picture for Talk Time and Real-World Reading
  • left / right picture cards
  • mini whiteboards or scrap paper
  • phone + small speaker, L1_L11_listening.mp3
  • Prep time: 30 min.

Key vocabulary (with pictures on the New Words page)

★ bank • ★ pharmacy • ★ park • ★ school • ★ store • ★ restaurant • ★ hospital • ★ bus stop • ★ street • ★ corner • left • right • map signs (EXIT, ONE WAY, PUSH)

Review

Is there a kitchen? Are there two bedrooms? (Lesson 10)

Clock-time plan

Times are loose. If a step runs long, take the time from Grammar or Talk Time. The last 15 minutes are Real-World Reading (Weeks 9–14).

7:10–7:15Exit Ticket + Homework5IndividualsNever skip
7:15–7:25Real-World Reading10Whole class → pairsTasks A–B only

Skip order if you're running behind: (1) the third play of the audio; (2) the pair drill at the end of Grammar; (3) half of Talk Time. Never skip: the listening tasks, the grammar boxes, and the exit ticket.

Attendance (15 → 7–8): every step lists both sizes. Print for the number you expect, plus 3 spares. Late arrivals join any pair right away.

Step by step

Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · Hello + Review · 10 min

  • Grouping: pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
  • Before class: write on the board: Is there a kitchen? Where's the bank? Go straight.
  • Model with one learner: "Is there a kitchen?" → "Yes, there is." Then mime: "Turn left."
  • Do: pairs use the Hello + Review page. Switch. Then find a new partner.
  • Homework check (last 3 min): partners show last week's homework. Walk around and look.
  • New learners: pair them with a strong partner.
  • If behind: one partner only.

Step 2 · 6:10–6:20 · New Words · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: point to map places: "Bank. Pharmacy. Park. School." Mime: "Go straight. Turn left. Turn right."
  • Do: point to each picture and say the word. Learners repeat twice. ★ words twice more.
  • Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then A asks Where's the ___? B answers with next to / across from.
  • If behind: teach the ★ words only.

Step 3 · 6:20–6:32 · Listening · 12 min

  • Grouping: individuals, then pairs check.
  • Before you listen (1 min): say: "Ana is on the street. She asks Marco for directions to the pharmacy."
  • Listen 1 → Task A. Listen 2 → Task B. Listen 3 → Task C.
  • Pairs compare after each task. Write answers on the board.
  • Say it: class repeats: Go straight two blocks. and It's next to the bank.
  • The audio plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen.
  • If behind: play 2 times; do Task C together.

Step 4 · 6:32–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 13 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs.
  • Show: Grammar page. Left = question. Right = answer. Point left, then right.
  • Box 1: Where's the bank? → It's on Main Street.
  • Box 2: It's next to / across from / between…
  • Box 3: Go straight. Turn left. Turn right. Mime each one.
  • Check questions: "The pharmacy is ___ the bank." (next to) • "Turn ___ at the corner." (left)
  • Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks Where's the…? B answers from the map; then A gives one direction.
  • If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices the same language.

Break · 6:45–7:00 · 15 min

  • Write on the board: Where's the…? It's next to… Go straight. Turn left. Turn right. Put map pages ready.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:10 · Talk Time · 10 min

  • Grouping: A–B pairs. Student A has the map (does not show it at first if you want an information gap).
  • Part 1 (5 min): B asks Where's the ___? A answers from the map (next to / across from / between). Three places.
  • Part 2 (4 min): B asks for directions to one place; A says Go straight… Turn… Then switch.
  • If behind: one round / half of Talk Time only.

Step 6 · 7:10–7:15 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP

  • Exit ticket: each learner says Where's the ___? or Go straight / Turn left.
  • Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 line 1 together. Point to each instruction.

Real-World Reading · 7:15–7:25 · Street Map + Signs · 10 min

  • Grouping: whole class, then pairs. Use the Real-World Reading page.
  • See it (2 min): Task A — find places on the map.
  • Hear it (2 min): say Turn left; learners point to LEFT sign / picture.
  • Read it (4 min): Tasks B–C — signs (EXIT, ONE WAY, PUSH); follow one written direction.
  • Partners: A gives a direction; B points on the map.
  • Learners who can't read yet: they point to pictures and say key words with everyone.
  • If behind: Tasks A and B only.

Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min

  • Grouping: individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
  • Part A: read the items in the answer key, slowly, 2 times each. Learners circle.
  • Parts B and C: match and write on their own. Help with instructions only.
  • Part D: read each "I can…" line; learners check one face.
  • Collect if you want. These checks are light practice, not a test grade.
  • If behind: do it next week at 6:00.

Listening script: L1_L11_listening.mp3 (about 1:10; the conversation plays once, so play the audio again if needed)

Audio: play from a phone + small speaker. No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Invented streets (Main Street). No real city names required.

Narrator: Lesson eleven. Listening. Ana is on the street. She asks Marco for directions to the pharmacy. Listen.

Ana: Excuse me. Where's the pharmacy?

Marco: It's on Main Street.

Ana: How do I get there?

Marco: Go straight two blocks.

Ana: Go straight two blocks. OK.

Marco: Then turn left at the corner. It's next to the bank.

Ana: Turn left at the corner. Next to the bank.

Marco: Yes. It's across from the park.

Ana: Across from the park. Is it near the school?

Marco: Yes, it is. The school is on the same street, between the park and the store.

Ana: Between the park and the store. Thank you so much!

Marco: You're welcome. Have a nice day!

Ana: You too. Bye!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

Listening A: 1 left 2 bank 3 park. B: Main Street. C: Go straight; Turn left (not Turn right). Grammar practice: 1 across from (or next to) 2 across from 3 between 4 left 5 left (or right) 6 answers will vary Real-World Reading A: 1 pharmacy 2 pharmacy. B: EXIT–b ONE WAY–c PUSH–a. C: 1 Go straight 2 Turn left. D: partner practice (no written key). Progress Check A (teacher reads twice): 1 bank 2 left 3 park 4 pharmacy 5 school B: 1–c 2–d 3–b 4–a C: 1 across from 2 between 3 next to Scoring: A /5 + B /4 + C /3 = /12. Not a test grade.

Teacher notes

  • Invented streets. Homework: look at a map on paper or phone — do not require walking alone.
  • Big mistake this week: in the left / mixing next to and across from. Mime and point.
  • Left/right: stand with the class facing the same way before you mime.
  • Learners who can't read yet: they point on the map and say place names.

Manager: That's OK. Can you start on Monday?

Ana: Yes, I can. Thank you so much!

Manager: You're welcome. See you Monday at nine.

Ana: See you Monday. Bye!

Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Answer key

Listening A: cook ✓; clean tables ✓; weekends ✓; night ✓; computer ✗ (but can learn); start Monday ✓. B: use a computer. C: Saturday, Sunday; Monday at nine. Grammar practice: 1 can 2 can't 3 Can 4 can 5 can't 6–7 answers will vary Real-World Reading A: 1 Name (the Name line) 2 Phone (the Phone line). B: answers will vary (skills check). C: answers will vary (I can… / I can't…). D: partner practice (no written key). Progress Check A (teacher reads twice): 1 cook 2 drive 3 computer 4 clean 5 swim B: 1–b 2–a 3–c 4–d C: 1 can 2 can't 3 Can Scoring: A /5 + B /4 + C /3 = /12. Not a test grade.

Teacher notes

  • Invented interview. Learners may invent skills.
  • Graduation talk (Week 16): prepare 3 sentences this week; reading from paper is fine.
  • Big mistake: I can to cook / I can cooking. Point to Grammar Box 2.
  • Manager voice in audio is Sam (not Carlos) for pitch stability.
  • Learners who can't write yet: they say Yes, I can and check boxes on the form.
